lawyer:
Choudhury Murshed Kamal Tipu, Advocate with AK Khan Uzzal, Advocate and Shah Navila Kashphi, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Md Nurul Amin, Advocate—For the Opposite. Party No. 1(a)-1(g).
parties:
Abdul Ahad (Md) --------- Petitioner
vs
Fazlur Rahman and others -------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
In an application under section 115(1) of Code of Civil Procedure, Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 16-5-2017 passed by the Special District Judge, Sylhet in Miscellaneous Appeal (Pre-emption) No. 53 of 2013, dismissing the appeal thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 26-6-2013 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Golapgonj, Sylhet in Miscellaneous Case (Pre-emption) being No. 15 of 2004 allowing the pre-emption, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.
2. The facts giving rise for disposal of the this Civil Revision, in a nutshell, can be stated that the case land originally belonged to three brothers namely Mahbubs Samad Choudhury, Mahfujus Samad Choudhury and Azizus Samad Choudhury. The owners of the case land were Mahbubs Samad Choudhury, Mahfujus Samad Choudhury and Azizuz Samad Choudhury. AfteriA ards Mahbub died leaving behind 4 sons—Akhlakus Samad Choudhury, Olius Samad Choudhury, Wasikus Sada t Choudhury and Safikus Samad Choudhury (OP No.4) and 3 daughters namely Asma, Ismat and Fayeka, (OP No. 12). Among them Akhlak sold out the entire share of Mahbub to Shahed on 24-9-79. Aziz died leaving behind 2 sons-Shajahan, Misfak and 4 daughters that are OP Nos. 24-27. Among them Shajahan has sold out the entire share of Aziz to Shahed on 23-12-80. Thus Shahed became the owner of 2/3rd share of the suit khatians by way of purchase and his father Mahfuj remained the owner of rest 1/3rd share. Later on both of them sold out 0.61 acres land to the Pre-emptor Fozlur Rahman and his brother Sofor Uddin (OP No. 28) on 28-11-81. Then Pre-emptee No.2 Abdul Ahad and his father filed pre-emption case No. 37/82 which was disallowed on contest on 14-8-86. Thereafter, Title Appeal and Civil Revision were also disallowed. Shahed and his father Mahfuj sold the rest 0.12 acres land to the Pre-emptor and his brother Pre-emptee No.28 on 31-3-02. Thus the Pre-emptor and his brother are in possession of the entire land by way of purchase within the knowledge of all of the persons concerned. Thereafter the pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 have purchased some the suit land from Pre-emptee No. 4 on 11-4-04 by a registered deed of purchase beyond the knowledge of the Pre-emptor. The petitioner came into know of the sale for the first time on 11-4-2004 and filed the pre-emption case on the basis of co-sharer by purchase.
3. On the other hand pre-emptee No. 2, by filing a written objection, contested this case and contending in short inter alia that there is no cause of action of for filing this case, it is barred by estoppel, waiver and acquiescence and limitation and bad for defect of parties and not maintainable in the present form. Denying all of the material facts of the plaint he stated that admittedly the owners of the case land were Mahbub, Mahfuj and Aziz. Afterwards Mahbub died leaving behind 4 sons namely Akhlak, Olius, Wasikus and Safik and 3 daughters Asma, Ismat and Fayeka, (Pre-emptee No. 12). Among them Shafikus Samad Choudhury got the entire case land in his possession by way of amicable partition. Later on he has sold the land to pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 on 19-1-04 within the knowledge of all the persons concerned. The deeds of purchase in favour Shahed as described in the petition are forged, collusive and ineffective. Moreover Akhlak and Sahjahan had no right to sale out the share of their brothers and sisters. Further the case is bad for defect of parties as the heirs of pre-emptee No. 1 are not made parties into the case. Besides pre-emptee No. 3 has been living in Saudi Arabia and he received no summon, notice of the case. The petitioner has filed the case with false statements and the same is liable to be dismissed.
4. The learned trial court during the trial of the pre-emption case after framing three issues, decided all the issues in favour of the pre-emptor on contest by its judgment and order dated 26-6-2013.
5. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order, the Pre-emptee No. 2 preferred an Miscellaneous Appeal (Pre-emption) being No. 53 of 2013 before the court of learned District Judge, Sylhet which was heard by Special District Judge, Sylhet and was ultimately dismissed by the judgment and order dated 16-5-2017, thereby affirming those passed by the trial court.
6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order the pre-emptee No. 2 appellant petitioner have preferred this Revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained Rule.
7. During hearing of the Rule, Mr Choudhury. Murshed Kamal Tipu, Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr Md Nurul Amin, Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite party No 1.
8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned appellate court below during disposal of the appeal committed illegality and irregularity. He further submits that the findings and decision .of the appellate court is based on misreading and non-reading of evidences and non consideration of material facts, thereby affirmed the judgment passed by the trial court, which resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learning advocate also submits that, the trial court at the time of disposal of the original pre-emption case without proper assessment of evidence and without appreciation of law decided the merit of the case in favour of the pre-emptor, and the lower appellate court without assigning his independent reasons affirmed that judgment and order. The learned advocate submits that pursuant to the section 96(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, all of the transferees shall be made parties. In the impugned registered deed of sale dated 23-2-2004 there are three transferees namely Md Ataur Rohman, Md Abdul Ahad and Md Layek Ahmed, though they have been impleaded as pre-emptees in the pre-emption case, but there were no valid Service of summons upon the pre-emptee No. 1 and 3 under Order V, rule 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure, .as they live outside the country. Mr Tipu further submits that pre-emptee No. 1 Md Ataur Rahman lives permanently in UK with his family and no valid service of summons were made upon him at his address in UK at all, and that's why he could not contest in the case. Pre-emptor of the case neither substituted the legal heirs of the pre-emptee No. 1 after his death under Order 22 Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure nor there were valid service summon under Order V Rule 25 and the trial court proceeded with the case in violation of the Code of Civil Procedure. The lower appellate court erred in law by relying on the Order XXII, rule 4(4) instead of the Order XXII, rule 4(1) and (3) as regards the substitution of the legal heirs of the pre-emptee No. 1 Md Ataur Rohman. Pre-emptee No. 3 Md Layek Ahmod lives in Saudi Arabia but it is admitted by the pre-emptor that no service of summons were made at his Saudi Arabia's address. A fraud practice was committed upon the court in the service of summons upon the pre-emptee No. 1 and 3. The PW 1 admitted during cross-examination that he did not take any steps for the substitution of the heirs of pre-emptee No. 1 namely Md Ataur Rohman who died in London, he also admitted that pre-emptee No. 3 lives in Saudi Arabia and he did not serve notice upon him at his address in Saudia Arabia. Learned counsel also submits that the question as to the service of summons were raised at in the written objection of the pre-emptee No. 2 at his earliest opportunity. Finally he submits that judgment and order of pre-emption obtained by suppressing summons is a judgment and order obtained fraudulently and, as such, nullity. In support of his submission he relied on the principles of law as set out in the decision reported in 12 BLC (AD) 79, 32 DLR (AD) 167, 2013 BLD (AD) 57 = 65 DLR (AD) 4 and 26 DLR 3. Accordingly, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the impugned judgment and order suffers from material illegality and irregularity which deserves interference by this court.
9. On contrary learned Advocate Mr Md Nurul Amin for the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 controverting the arguments advanced from the learned advocate for the petitioner, and opposing the Rule by submitting that the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal and deciding the merit of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned counsel further submits that the finding and decision of the appellate courts is based on proper appreciation of evidence on record. Learned counsel submits that the issue raised by the present petitioner that the pre-emption case is not maintainable as the legal heirs of the pre-emptee No. 1 Md Ataur Rahman were not substituted is not tenable in the eye of law because the pre-emptee No. 1 contested the case by filing the written statement but he did not contest the case anymore, and, as such, it is not necessary to substitute his legal heirs pursuant to Order 22 Rule 4(4) of the Civil Procedure Code. Learned counsel further submits that any objection as to omission of a necessary party must be taken at the earliest opportunity; if not so taken, may be deemed to have been waived. The pre-emption case cannot be failed for non joinder of parties. The pre-emptor prayed for supplying the foreign address of the pre-emptee No. 1 which was allowed by the trial court but the pre-emptee No. 2 failed to provide the address, and, as such, the pre-emptee No. 2 present petitioner is debarred from raising the point of defect of parties. The petitioner did not challenge the trial court's order No. 17 dated 5-6-2006 accepting the service of notice upon the pre-emptee No. 3 Md Layek Ahmed. Mr Md Nurul Amin for the opposite parties, in support of his submission referred to the decision 51 DLR 554, 31 DLR (AD) 88, 49 DLR (AD) 151, 12 MLR (AD) 120, 58 DLR (AD) 159 and 50 DLR 441.Finally he submits that the mere error of law is not ground for interfere in a revisional jurisdiction, unless the error of law caused occasioning failure of justice, accordingly he prays for discharge of the Rule.
10. In order to appreciate the submission advanced from the sides of the learned counsels for the respective parties, having gone through the judgment passed by the trial court, the impugned judgment and order passed by the appellate court below, the pleading of the parties and the evidences led from the respective parties, along with the case records, it transpires that the instant opposite party No. 1 filed the pre-emption case under section 96 of the SAT Act as a co-sharer by purchase impugning the registered deed of transfer dated 23-2-2004 (Exhibit No. 2 gha) in favour of three brothers.
11. Having gone through the case records it appears that PW 1 Md Fazlur Rohman categorically testified in support of his case. During the cross-examination he replied—
“....... তিনটি দাগে নালিশী ভূমি” ২৬৮১ দাগে মোট জায়গা ২৯ শতক, এই দাগে কতটুকু জায়গা অগ্রক্রয় চাই তা সুনির্দিষ্ট বলতে পারব না ।......আমি পরে শুনি ১নং তরফছানী ১১-৮-০৭ ইং তারিখ লন্ডনে মারা যান। ৪ ছেলে, ৪ মেয়ে, ১ স্ত্রী রেখে মারা যান কিনা আমি জানি না। তার উত্তরাধীকারীদের আমি পক্ষ করি নাই মামলায় । ইনং তরফছানী কি জবাব দেয় মামলায় তা আমি পড়ি নাই। ......৩নং তরফছানী সৌদি আরব থাকে। তার সৌদি আরবের ঠিকানা দেই নাই ।...... কোন দাগে কত পরিমান জায়গা অগ্রক্রুয় প্রার্থনা করি তা পৃথকভাবে বলতে পারব না।......”
12. OPW 1 Md Abdul Ahad deposed in support of his case, among of which he stated—
“....... আমার ভাই ১নং তরফছানী যুক্তরাজ্যে থাকাবস্থায় ১১-৮-০৭ তারিখে মারা যান ৪ ছেলে, ৪ মেয়ে ও স্ত্রী রেখে। তার মৃত্যু সনদের কপি দাখিল করেছি। ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ থেকে উত্তরাধিকারী সনদ ও মৃত্যু সনদ দাখিল করেছি। ১নং তরফছানী কোন সমন নোটিশ পায়নি । তার স্ত্রী ছেলে মেয়েকে পক্ষ করা হয়নি। ৩নং তরফছানী সৌদি আরব থাকেন, তিনি ও সমন নোটিশ পান নি ।......”
13. It also transpires from the written objection dated 4-11-2008 filed by the pre-emptee No. 2 Md Abdul Ahad that he raised the issue in the said written objection that pre-emptee No. 1 Md Ataur Rohman who lived in London, no service notice and summons were made at his address in London and after his death his legal heirs were neither made parties, nor they received any notice or summons. Pre-emptee No. 3 Layek Ahmod has been living in Saudi Arabia, but no service of notice and summons were made to his address in Saudi Arabia. Having gone through the case records it appears that wakalatnama was executed on 21-7-2004 by pre-emptee No. 2 Md Abdul Ahad only and he submitted the written objection. No one else except the pre-emptee No. 2 neither filed wokalatnama nor they submitted written objection.
<u>14. It is also evident from the trial court's order No. 8 dated 1-8-2005 where the learned trial judge directed upon the pre-emptee No. 2 to provide with the foreign address of the pre-emptee No. 1, but no order of the trial court shows that he directed to provide with the address of the pre-emptee No. 3 namely Md Layed Ahmed. But astonishingly from the trial court's order No. 17 dated 5-6-2006 which states  “...... আগামী ৫-৯-২০০৬ ইং তারিখ আপত্তি দাখিল । ধার্য তাং ৩/২৪ নং তরফছানীর এ/ডি ফেরত । পরবর্তীতে দেখা যায় যে, ৩নং তরফছানীর এডি ফেরত আসিয়াছে ।......" In the record there is nothing to indicate that service of summons was made upon the pre-emptee No. 3 at his address in Saudi Arabia, nor the acknowledgment due (A/D) was received by the trial court from the pre-emptee No. 3 who lives in Saudi Arabia. Above all, the pre-emptor admitted in his cross-examination that he did not serve any summons upon the pre-emptee No. 3 at the address in Saudia Arabia. Accordingly it is not safe to rely on statutory presumption of service of summon, upon the pre-emptee No. 3 within the meaning of Order V Rule 19 B(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the present case a judgment and order of pre-emption was obtained which indicates that a fraud was committed upon the court in the service of summon upon the pre-emptee No. 3. When a fraud is proved, then that fraud vitiates everything.</u>
15. The principle of law settled in 32 DLR (AD) 167 it was held that a judgment and decree obtained by suppressing summon is a decree obtained fraudulently and, as such, nullity and the decree which has been questioned in the present Miscellaneous Appeal, is a nullity.
16. In 12 BLC (AD) 79 the principle of was settled that where a judgment obtained which indicates that a fraud was committed upon the court as well as upon the defendants and when, a fraud is proved then the court is not debarred to interfere under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
17. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above, I am constrained to hold such a view that the submissions advanced from the learned counsel Mr Choudhury Murshed Kamal Tipu on behalf of the petitioner have got sufficient merit and substance, which are well founded and consistent with the case records.
18. In the result, the Rule having merit is made absolute without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 16-5-2017 passed by the Special District Judge, Sylhet in Miscellaneous Appeal (Pre-emption) No. 53 of 2013, dismissing the appeal thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 26-6-2013 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Golapgonj, Sylhet in Miscellaneous Case (Pre-emption) being No. 15 of 2004 is hereby set-aside.
19. The order of stay granted at the issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.
Communicate the judgment and order at once and send back the lower courts' record immediately.
End.

lawyer:
Abdur Rafique, Advocate for Sheikh Md Maju Miah—For the Petitioner.  
 Nakib Saiful Islam with Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain, Advocates—For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Abdul Khaleque (Md) --------- Petitioner
Vs.
Popular Life Insurance Company Limited --------- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Bhishmadev Chakrabortty, J: This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order of the Joint District Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka passed in Money Suit No. 60 of 2004 on 1-4-2015 rejecting the petitioner's application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that the opposite party instituted the aforesaid money suit in the Court of Joint District Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka for realization of Taka 9,54,548. This petitioner as defendant appeared in the suit and filed written statement to contest it. In course of time its date was fixed to 25-3-2014 for ex-parte hearing. The learned Judge examined one witness for the plaintiff on that day and decreed the suit as prayed for. The defendant then filed an application purportedly under Order 9 rule 13A of the Code for setting the ex-parte decree. The Joint District Judge allowed the application on 10-11-2014 subject to the payment of cost (CP cost) of Taka 3,000 to be paid within ten working days with default order and set-aside the ex-parte decree. The petitioner, however, failed to comply with the Court's order and filed an application under section 151 of the Code to the concerned Court on 19-3-2015 praying for accepting the CP cost by condoning the delay of 114 days. The Joint District Judge rejected the said application holding that for non payment of the CP cost within the time prescribed by the Court, the order has been set-aside automatically. Being aggrieved by, the defendant petitioner approached this Court and obtained the present rule.
3. Mr Abdur Rafique, learned Advocate appearing for Sheikh Md Maju Miah for the petitioner refers the provisions of section 148 and 151 of the Code and submits that under section 148 of the Code, a civil Court has jurisdiction to extent the period for depositing the CP cost and can enlarge the period from time to time, even the time fixed by it has been expired. Mr Abdur Rafique refers to the cases of Idris Shaikh vs jilamaun Bewa and others, 50 DLR (AD) 161; Abu Sama vs Abu Syed and others, 48 DLR 141 and the case of Wajeda Khatun and others vs Saonatun Bewa, 55 DLR 460 and submits that in view of the ratio laid in the aforesaid cases, a Court in appropriate cases can extent the time for submitting CP cost. In the instant case, the learned Joint District Judge in not allowing the application under section 151 of the Code committed error of law resulting in an error in such order occasioning of failure of justice, which can be interfered with by this Court.
4. Mr Nakib Saiful Islam, learned Advocate appearing with Mr Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain opposes the rule and submits that the Court after passing the default order had become functus officio after expiry of the period fixed by it and had no jurisdiction to entertain the petitioner's application under section 151 of the Code. The order passed by the Joint District Judge allowing the application under Order 9 rule 13A of the Code with costs to be paid within ten days, with default order, has become final after expiry of the time and ex-parte decree passed earlier stands. He refers to the cases of MM Ibrahim vs Mizanul Hague Chowdhury and others, 69 DLR (AD) 192 and Parvin Akter and others vs Eastern Bank Limited and others, 70 DLR (AD) 117 and relying on the ratio laid in those cases submits that to pass an order on an application the proceeding has to be pending before it. In the instant case, for the default order, there was no proceeding before the Court pending, and, as such, the Court cannot pass any order upon it by accepting the
CP cost and to restore the suit to its original file. In view of the above, this Rule having no merit would be discharged.
5. We have considered the submissions of both the parties, gone through the rule petition and annexure appended thereto.
6. It appears that in the application under Order 9 rule 13A of the Code the petitioner has taken grounds that their tadbirkar had been seriously ill and for it he failed to collect the date of the suit. He could not conduct the appointed Advocate and consequently failed to appear before the Court on the day when it was fixed and called on for hearing. He would suffer irreparable loss and injury, if the case is not restored to the file and number. Since the application under Order 9 rule 13A of the Code was within the period of limitation, the Joint District Judge allowed it with cost to be paid with 10 (ten) working days with default order. But the petitioner failed to deposit the cost within the time prescribed by the Court. He then filed an application under section 151 of the Code to extent the time for depositing the cost which was rejected by the Joint District Judge.
7. Section 148 of the Code reads as follows—
"Where any period is fixed or granted by the Court for the doing any act prescribed or allowed by this Code, the Court may, in its discretion, from time to time, enlarge such period, even though the period originally fixed or granted may have expired".
<u>8. On going through the above provisions of the Code, we find that the time fixed by the Court for payment of CP cost, even with default order, can be extended from time to time in appropriate cases. In this case, we find that the petitioner filed written statement in the suit to contest it, but unfortunately he could not appear in the Court when it was called on for hearing and consequently it was decreed ex-parte. Subsequently, the said ex-parte decree was set-aside on m application of the petitioner with cost and default order. The petitioner defaulted in payment and then filed the application under section 151 of the Code. Under inherent jurisdiction, the Court ought to have allowed the petitioner's application for depositing the cost giving him a chance to contest the suit. In this context, the ratio of the case reported in 50 DLR (AD) 161 referred to by Mr Rafique can be relied upon. We do not find any substance in the submission of Mr Islam that the Court has become functus officio or it had no jurisdiction to entertain the application under section 151 of the Code. In the cases where the time limit for depositing any amount has been fixed by the statute, there the Court cannot extent its hand as per the provision of section 148 of the Code. The cases referred to by Md Islam reported in 70 DLR (AD) 117 and 69 DLR (AD) 192 do not apply in the case in hand considering the facts of those cases upon which the ratio was laid.</u>
9. In view of above discussion, we find merit in this rule, accordingly the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order passed by the Joint District Judge, Dhaka is hereby set-aside. The Joint District Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka is directed to accept the CP cost deposited by the petitioner, if not deposited, the petitioner is directed to deposit it within 10 (ten) working days from the date of receipt of this judgment and order. The learned Joint District Judge is directed to proceed with Money Suit No. 60 of 2004 and dispose of it expediciously, preferably within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order.
Communicate this judgment and order to the concerned Court.
End.

Sarder Shafiqul Islam --------- Appellant
VS

full_judgment:
Md Badruzzaman, J: This appeal is directed against judgment and decree dated 13-4-2004 (decree signed on 20-4-2004) passed by learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Suit No. 61 of 2004 rejecting the plaint under Order VII, rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
2. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of this appeal, are that the appellant and another as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 61 of 2004 in 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Khulna praying for a decree of declaration that all proceedings including auction sale dated 29-4-2004 as well as delivery of possession dated 26-7-2004 in Title Execution Case No. 61 of 1996 of the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna (arising out of decree dated 17-1-1988 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 166 of 1985 of the Court of District Judge, Khulna) are malafide, illegal, unlawful, effective, without any lawful authority, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs.
3. The case of the plaintiffs, as is made out in the plaint, is that the property described in schedule 'B' of the plaint was originally belonged to Dr. Noor Uddin Ahmed and his wife Most. Jobeda Khatoon and they transferred the same by three registered sale deeds being No. 6125 dated 14-3-1983, No. 6415 dated 16-3-1983 and No. 7224 dated 27-3-1983 in favour of Sarder Kawser Uddin Ahmed, SM Rabiul Islam and SM Nazrul Islam (plaintiff No. 2) and delivered possession thereof to them and since then they had been residing therein. SM Rabiul Islam and Sarder Kawser Uddin have died and their heirs are plaintiff No. 1 and defendants Nos. 13-23. Said Noor Uddin Ahmed and his wife Jobeda Khatoon mortgaged the suit property to defendant No. 2 Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation (In-short HBFC) against housing loan obtained from HBFC and to realize the loan, HBFC filed Miscellaneous Case No. 166 of 1985 in the Court of learned District Judge, Khulna which was decreed vide judgment and decree dated 17-1-1988. Said decree dated 17-1-1988 was put to execution in Title Execution Case No. 14 of 1989 in 3rd Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Khulna which was dismissed on 20-7-1990. Defendant No. 2 then filed Second Execution Case No. 61 of 1996 on 27-6-1996 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna which was barred by limitation but the Execution Court, without dismissing the case, condoned the delay without having jurisdiction to condone such delay. In course of execution process in Title Execution Case No. 61 of 1996, the suit property was put to auction on 29-4-2004 and defendant No. 1 purchased the property in auction at a consideration of Taka 7,48,000 though the property was valued at least Taka 20,00,000 at the relevant time. Having learnt about the same, the plaintiffs appeared in the title execution case on 26-7-2004 and prayed for staying the execution proceedings but the same was rejected. Defendant No. 1 auction purchaser came to take possession of the suit property on 26-7-2004 and found all the rooms of the building under lock and key and accordingly, he could not take possession of the suit property. The plaintiffs and their co-sharers have been residing in the suit property as usual. The execution case was proceeded by suppression of summons and the Execution Court had no jurisdiction to proceed with the execution case, as such, the plaintiffs have filed the present suit challenging the execution proceedings.
4. Defendant No. 1 auction purchaser on 10-8-2004 filed written statement and defendant No. 2 HBFC filed written statement on 25-8-2004. The cases of the defendants are more or less same. They contended that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; that there is no cause of action of the suit; that the plaintiffs have no locus stnndi to file the suit and the suit is barred by limitation as well as under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Their positive case is that the suit land belonged to Dr. Noor Uddin Ahmed and his wife Jobeda Khatoon and while they were owner in possession thereof took loan from defendant No. 2 HBFC for construction of residential building therein and as security of the loan they mortgaged the suit land vide two registered mortgage deeds being Nos. 20559 dated 21-12-1978 and 15011 dated 11-8-1979 and they constructed residential building in the suit land with the loan money obtained from HBFC. Since the mortgagors failed to repay the loan amount with interest, defendant No. 2 HBFC filed Miscellaneous Case No. 166 of 1985 in the Court of learned District Judge, Khulna under provision of PO 7 of 1973 against the borrowers for realization of the outstanding dues and the miscellaneous case was allowed ex-parte on 17-1-1988. Thereafter, defendant No. 2 decree-holder filed Execution Case No. 14 of 1989 before the learned District Judge, Khulna who transferred the same to the then Commercial Court, Khulna for disposal but the miscellaneous case was dismissed for default on 20-7-1990. After dismissal of aforesaid case defendant No. 2 filed Second Execution Case No. 61 of 1996 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna and after due service of all process of the execution case, the mortgaged property was put to auction and defendant No. 1 purchased the property in auction on 29-4-2004 at a consideration of Taka 7,48,000 following which the sale was confirmed on 30-5-2004 and the auction purchaser took delivery of possession of the suit property through Court on 26-7-2004 with the aid of police forces and process server. After taking possession, the auction purchaser is owning and possessing the suit property.
5. It has also stated that the alleged sale deeds of the plaintiffs are null and void deeds because of the fact that the mortgagors had no right to transfer the suit property without prior permission of defendant No. 2 HBFC and accordingly, the plaintiffs have or had acquired no right, title or interest in the suit property. In order to frustrate the auction purchaser's right, title and possession, the plaintiffs have filed the suit.
6. After filing the written statement, defendant No. 1, auction purchaser; on 6-1-2005 filed an application under Order Vii, rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the plea that the suit is barred under provision of section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and the Court has no jurisdiction to proceed with the suit. The plaintiffs did not file any written objection against the application. The trial Court, after hearing the parties, vide order dated 13-4-2005 rejected the plaint holding that the suit is barred under section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Following which the decree was drawn up on 20-4-2004.
7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 13-4-2005, plaintiff No. 1 has preferred the instant appeal.
8. Respondent No. 1 alone, respondent Nos. 13-16 jointly and respondent Nos. 4-12 and 14 jointly filed Voklatnama to contest the appeal.
9. Mr Ahmed Nowshed Jamil, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submits that the trial Court upon misconception of law rejected the plaint without considering the true perspective of the provisions under section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Learned Advocate further submits that no summons or process of the miscellaneous case and execution case was served upon the borrowers/judgment debtors. Learned Advocate further submits that the judgment was pronounced by the learned District Judge under provisions of PO 7 of 1973 and the District Judge had only jurisdiction to execute the decree and the Artha Rin Adalat had no jurisdiction to execute the decree or order passed by the learned District Judge in miscellaneous proceeding under PO 7 of 1973 and accordingly, all the proceedings commenced by the Artha Rin Adalat are nullity in the eye of law and accordingly, the auction purchaser acquired no right, title or interest in the suit property. Learned Advocate further submits that the provisions under Artha Rin Adalat Ain does not specifically or impliedly debar a citizen to establish his title to in a civil Court in respect of any property which has been mortgaged with a financial institution. Learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs are third party claimants and they have right to file suit under Order XXI, rule 103 of the Code of Civil procedure and this provision can be applied even after exhausting remedies provided under rules 98, 99 and 101 of Order 21 of the Code. Learned Advocate further submits that the financial institution like Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation has two options to realize the loan from the defaulter borrower, one is an application before the District Judge under article 27 of the President Order 7 of 1973 by depositing a very nominal court fee applicable to the applications and the other is by filing regular suit before the Artha Rin Adalat upon deposition ad valorem court-fee and the Artha Rin Adalat will only has jurisdiction in such a case if the concerned financi.al institution has filed a suit before it upon depositing ad valorem court fee for realization of loan, and this position of law has already been settled by the Apex Court in various decisions. Learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case the House Building Finance Corporation-got decree against the borrowers by application filed under Article 27 of PO 7 of 1973 from the District Judge but it filed second execution case before the Artha Rin Adalat and the Adalat proceeded with the execution case and sold the mortgage property in auction without having jurisdiction to do so and, as such, all proceedings in Title Execution Case No. 61 of 1996 are nullity in the eye of law.
10. In support of his contention learned Advocate has referred to the cases of Mohanznzad Gias Uddin Chozvdhury and others vs Bangladesh and others 8 LM (AD) 322, Government of Bangladesh and others vs Basaratullah and others, 1989 BLD 97 = 40 DLR 554 and Abdu! Mukid (Md) vs Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna and another 66 DLR 211.
11. As against the above contention, Mr Md Mahbub Ali, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 1, auction purchaser, submits that admittedly, before so called purchase by the plaintiffs the suit property was mortgaged to House Building Finance Corporation and, as such, the subsequent transfers by the mortgagors to plaintiff No. 2 and others cannot be treated as valid and legal transfer and those transfers did not create any right, title or interest in favour of the plaintiffs. Learned Advocate further submits that after mortgaging the property in question to Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, subsequent transfers of the same to the plaintiff No. 2 and predecessors of plaintiff No.1 and defendant Nos. 13-23 by the mortgagors without the consent of the mortgagee and without repaying the loan is nothing, but a fraudulent act and it is by now well settled that fraud vitiates everything. Learned Advocate further submits that in view of the provisions under rule 103 of Order 21 of the Code, the plaintiffs did not have locus standi to file the suit challenging the execution proceeding. Learned Advocate further submits that the suit is not maintainable because the plaintiffs have no right, title or interest in the suit property and, as such, the trial Court committed no illegality in rejecting the plaint. In support of his contention learned Advocate has referred to the cases of Syed Jubayer Hossain vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka and others 28 BLC (AD) 50 and Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and Assistant Custodian, Vested and Non-Resident Property vs Tohidul Hossain Choudhury and others 51 DLR (AD) 117.
12. We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the plaint, written statements, application filed under Order VII rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the impugned order passed by the trial Court and other materials available on record.
13. On perusal of the plaint of Title Suit No. 61 of 2004 it appears that the plaintiffs at paragraph 1-2 of the plaint stated that Dr. Noor Uddin Ahmed and his wife Jobeda Khatoon were owners of the suit property who transferred the same by three registered sale deeds dated 14-3-1983, 16-3-1983 and 27-3-1983 in favour of plaintiff No. 2 and two others (predecessors of plaintiff No. 1 and defendant Nos. 13-23) and that Dr. Noor Uddin Ahmed and his wife Jobeda Khatoon mortgaged their properties to defendant No. 2 Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation against loan obtained by them and the defendant No. 2 got decree on 10-1-1988 in Miscellaneous Case No. 116 of 1985 against the mortgagors.
14. Admittedly, the suit property was mortgaged by the real owners Dr. Noor Uddin Ahmed and his wife Most. Jobeda Khatoon to Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation against loan obtained by them and they executed and registered two mortgage deeds dated 21-12-1978 and 4-8-1979. The plaintiffs claimed that said Dr. Noor Uddin Ahmed and his wife Most. Jobeda Khatoon transferred said property by three registered sale deeds in 1983. It has also stated that Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation filed miscellaneous Case No. 166 of 1985 before the learned District Judge, Khulna and got decree against the mortgagors on 17-1-1988. The plaintiffs did not state anything in the plaint as to whether the judgment debtors have or had filed any appeal or any other proceeding challenging the said decree passed by the learned District Judge.
15. Now question arises whether the plaintiffs or their predecessors have acquired any right, title or interest in said mortgaged property by dint of their purchased deeds.
16. An immovable property which is given as a security against a loan is known as mortgaged property. Section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 stipulates that a mortgage is the transfer, of an interest in specific immovable property for the purpose of securing the payment of money advanced or to be advanced by way of loan or debt. Where, without delivering possession of the mortgaged property, the mortgagor binds himself personally to pay the mortgage-money, and agrees that in the event of his failing to pay according to his contract, the mortgagee shall have a right to cause the mortgage property to be sold and the proceeds of sale to be applied in payment of the mortgage-money, the transaction is called a simple mortgage and the mortgagee, a simple mortgagee.
17. In the instant case, the mortgagors did not deliver possession of the mortgaged property to the mortgagee but agreed to pay the loan amount and failing which they agreed that the mortgagee shall have the right to sale the property if they fail to repay the amount. Accordingly, this is a simple mortgage.
18. As per section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act the right of redemption is available to the mortgagor after the principal loan amount has become due and paid. Section 60A of the Transfer of Property Act allows the mortgagor to require the mortgagee to assign the mortgage debt and transfer mortgagor's property to such third party as the mortgagor may direct and the mortgagee shall be bound to obey such direction of the mortgagor.
19. Therefore, under section 60A of the Transfer of Property Act a transfer of mortgaged-property by sale in favour of third party can be made because the mortgagor is still the owner. However, when the third party would buy the property from the mortgagor, he will be buying the right to redemption because that is what mortgagor has with him. He can then redeem the property and enjoy subrogation. He cannot have better right then the mortgagor. It is the responsibility of the third party to make proper inquiry before purchasing the property from the mortgagor and ask him to clear the encumbrance.
20. Section 48 of the Transfer of Property Act deals with the doctrine of priority. It provides protection to the mortgagee from subsequent transactions created by the mortgagor over the same property. If a man creates subsequent interests in the same immovable property which cannot be enjoyed to their full extent or conflict each other, each right which is created after the prior one would be subjected to the previously created right unless there is some contract binding prior transferee. Thus, the mortgagor cannot prejudice the rights of the mortgagee by creating subsequent interests in the same immovable property. The mortgagor is capable of creating subsequent mortgage or sale the property if he has the title deed, but the doctrine of priority would not allow him to refrain the prior mortgagee from enjoying his rights. This is based upon the doctrine "first in time, first in law". Simply saying, the third party purchaser, after purchase of the mortgaged-property, steps into the shoes of the mortgagor.
21. From the record it reveals that after mortgaging the property in question in favour of the Bangladesh House Building Corporation in 1978 and 1979, the mortgagors allegedly transferred the property in question in favour of plaintiff No. 2 and two others in 1983 by executing and registering three sale deeds. In Syed Jubayer Hossain vs Artha Rin Adalat reported in 28 BLC (AD) 50 the Appellate Division held as follows:
"After mortgaging the property in question to the bank, subsequent transfer of the same to others without the consent of mortgagee bank by the mortgagor without the view of repaying the loan is nothing, but a fraudulent act and it is by now well settled that fraud vitiates everything."
<u>22. It is settled principle of law that when there is no right, there is no remedy. For the maintainability of a declaratory suit under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act the plaintiff must have a legal character or any right as to the property in suit. A person cannot sue for a declaration of his right unless he has an existing right. In the instant case, the mortgagors neither took permission from HBFC before the transfer was made to the plaintiffs nor repaid the loan amount before the transfer. As such, in view of the relevant provisions of Transfer of Property Act, as discussed above, as well the decision the Hon'ble Appellate Division in Syed Jubayer Hossain (supra) the transaction was a -fraudulent one and by dint of such transfer plaintiffs could not acquire right, title or interest in the suit property. Accordingly, their suit for declaration that the execution proceeding against their vendor-mortgagors was illegal, ineffective and not binding upon them is not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.</u>
23. Now another question arises whether, the plaintiffs can be considered as third party claimants and whether they have right to institute Suit under rule 103 of order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
24. In Md Sekandar and another vs Janata Bank Limited and others 3 LM (AD) 448 this issue has specifically decided. The plaintiffs of that suit were claiming title to in the mortgaged-property by way of purchase from Md Abul Kalam Chowdhury and Raja Miah and the judgment debtors mortgaged the property showing Md Khorshed Mia, Kashem Mia and Md Hossain as sons of Lal Miah, Chand Mia and Younus Mia, who had no sons under the name Md Khorshed Mia, Kashem Mia and Md Hossain. They prayed for declaration of title in respect of the suit land and they also prayed for declaration that the decree passed in Mortgage Suit No. 35 of 1995 was void and not binding upon them. The Appellate Division, after considering the plaintiffs as third-party claimants came to the conclusion that the said suit was maintainable. The Appellate Division in coming to such conclusion observed, "a third party claimant, who has right, title and interest in the decreetal property has limited scope to file objection against the attachment of the property in dispute or sale of the attached property in execution of a decree. He has also a right to file a suit under Order 21 rule 103 and this provision can be applied even after exhausting remedies provided in Rules 98, 99 and 101. Suit under Rule 103 is in the nature of a special remedy." The Appellate Division also took the view, "the scope of the suit under Order XXI, rule 103 is not merely to ascertain whether the plaintiff was in possession at the date of order against him, but the establishment of the right and title by which the plaintiff's claim to be in possession of the property. Therefore, in view of sub-section (1) of section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain that while a third party can pray for setting aside the decree or order, the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable, we find no cogent ground to prevent a third party to file a suit to establish his title to in the property sold in execution of a decree in view of Order 21 rule 103 since the said provision appears in Order 21 under the heading 'Execution of Decrees and Orders'."
25. The case of Sekandar, 3 LM (AD) 448 (supra) is quite distinguishable considering the facts and circumstances of the instant case because in the said case the third-party-claimants claimed their independent title to and possession in the suit property from the persons other than the mortgagors. In the instant case the plaintiffs are claiming their title to and possession in the suit property through the mortgagors. As such, the plaintiffs cannot be considered as third-party-claimants and accordingly, they have no remedy under rule 103 of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the auction process because" of the fact that the plaintiffs have stepped into the shoes of the mortgagors/judgment-debtors.
26. Now another question arises whether Artha Rin Adalot has jurisdiction to execute the decree passed by learned District Judge.
27. It appears that Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation got decree on 17-1-1988, the mortgaged property was sold in auction on 29-4-2004 which was confirmed on 30-5-2004 and the auction purchaser took delivery of possession of the suit property through Court on 26-7-2004. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed the suit challenging the execution proceeding as well as the auction process on the plea that the execution Court had no jurisdiction to execute the decree. We are unable to accept such contention because a transferee from mortgagor or judgment debtor is presumed to be aware of the mortgage of the property and the pendency of the proceeding before Court and he should be careful in purchasing a mortgage property. If any unfair, un-equitable or undeserved protection is afforded to a transferee from mortgagor, the decree holder will never be able to realize the fruits of the decree. Moreover, in Additional Deputy Commissioner vs Tohidul Hossain 51 DLR (AD) 117 it is held, " auction sale having taken place and the sale having been confirmed by issuance of the sale certificate in favour of the auction purchaser, such sale cannot be illegally withheld by parties not connected with the mortgage suit or with the mortgage execution case".
28. It appears from the impugned order that the trial Court rejected the plaint as being barred under section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Said section is quoted verbatim below:
“২০। এই আইনের বিধান ব্যতিরেকে, কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট অর্থ খণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন কার্যধারা বা উহার কোন আদেশ, রায় বা ডিক্রীর বিষয়ে কোন প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করা যাইবে না, এবং এই আইনের বিধানকে উপেক্ষা করিয়া কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আবেদন করিয়া কোন প্রকার দাবী বা প্রার্থনা করা হইলে, এরূপ আবেদন কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষ গ্রাহ্য করিবে না।”
29. From a plain reading of section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003, it appears that except the provisions of this Act, no question shall be raised before any Court or authority about any pending proceeding in the Artha Rin Adalat, or against its order, judgment or decree, and if any relief is claimed or prayed before any Court or authority ignoring the provisions of this Act, no Court or authority shall accept any such prayer. Section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain specifically debarred in filing of a separate suit against any order or decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat.
30. In the instant case, the appellant and another by filing the suit, have challenged the execution proceeding as well as auction process conducted by the Adalat on the ground of lack of jurisdiction and fraud. Section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 creates a clear bar in instituting such suit making such prayer even on the ground of fraud or lack of jurisdiction to execute the decree by the Adalat. Therefore, we are of the view that the trial Court committed no illegality in rejecting the plaint by the impugned judgment and decree as being barred by law.
31. Other cases, which have been cited by the learned Advocate for the appellant, are not applicable in this case because the facts and circumstances of those cases and those of the present one are distinguishable.
32. In view of the above, we find no merit in this appeal.
33. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, however without any order as to costs.
Send down the LCR along with a copy of this judgment to the Court below at once.
End.

lawyer:
Muhammad Jamiruddin Sircar with Md Zahirul Islam with Sahida Irin, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Md Giasuddin Ahammad, DAG Md Shahabuddin Ahmed, AAG with Md Shaifour Rahman Siddique, Advocate-For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Abdur Rahman Khan and others ------ Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioners
vs
Government of Bangladesh ------- Defendant-Appellant-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Hasan, J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the Opposite Party, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 3-2-2011 (decree signed on 8-2-2011), passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Rajbari, in Title Appeal No.104 of 2007, allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 8-8-2007 (decree signed on 12-8-2007), passed by the Assistant Judge (In charge), Goalanda, Rajbari, in Title Suit No. 33 of 2006, partly decreeing the suit, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. Facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, in brief are that, one Abdur Rahman Khan and 4 others, had filed Title Suit No. 33 of 2006, before the Assistant Judge, Goalanda, Rajbari, against the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajbari, alleging amongst other that, the property described in schedule to the plaint belonged to one Foyjuddin Sheikh and others of RS Plot No. 3206 of RS Khatian No. 771 of Mouza Uttor Uzanchar, PS Goalanda, Rajbari, and has been recorded in the name Foyjuddin Sheikh as Rayot to the extent of 8 annas share. Thereafter, during SA operation, the name of Foyjuddin Sheikh has been recorded as one of the tenants for 8 annas share in the suit property described schedule No. "Ka" including the suit Plot No. 3206, vide SA Khatian No. 772 of Mouza Uttor Ujanchar, PS Goalanda, Rajbari. It has also been stated that, Abdus Satter Sheikh, son of Foyjuddin Sheikh having succeeded to his father's property he has sold 81/4 decimals of land to Md Abdur Rahman Khan, vide deed No. 2021 dated 1-12-1986 (Exhibit 10). He has also sold 161/2 decimals of land to Md Abdul Motin Miah, vide deed No. 1946 dated 22-11-1986 (Exhibit 9). He next sold 141/2 decimals of land to Abdul Mojid Sheikh and his wife Jorina Begum, vide deed No. 704 dated 28-5-1990 (Exhibit 7). He also sold 51/2 decimals of land to the plaintiff No. 4 Bisha Sikder @ Bishu Sikder and, vide deed No. 2023 dated 1-12-1986 and he also sold 11/2 decimals of land to Bisha Sikder, vide deed No. 341 dated 15-3-2003 (Exhibit 5 and 6), respectively. It has also been stated that, the purchaser A fsar Ali Mollah has sold 8¼ decimals of land to the plaintiff No. 5 Md Helal Uddin Miah, vide deed No. 915 dated 27-5-1999 (Exhibit8) and that total 41 decimals of land out of 1.40 acre of land of RS Khatian No. 771 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 772 of the said Mouza. It has further been stated that, the Government has illegally recorded this RS/SA Plot No. 3206 in its name in khas Khatian No. 1 during BS operation as BS Plot No. 2510 and 2511 of Mouza Goalanda Ghat. Therefore, they have prayed for declaration of title in the suit property.

3. The defendant No. 1 i.e. the Government contested in the suit by filing written statements in which it has been stated that, the entire 41 decimals of land, lying at SA Plot No. 3206 of SA Khatian No. 772, was submerged into the river Padma in the natural course and subsequently reappeared in the said site. Thereafter, the said property of the SA Plot No. 3206 has been vested in the name of the Government as per provision of PO 135 of 1972 and has been recorded in the khas khatian No. 1 of the Mouza Goalanda Ghat as BS Plot No. 2510 and 2511. Therefore, the previous SA record has no existence and the Government has rightly recorded the same and the plaintiffs have no right, title in the suit property. It has prayed for dismissal of the suit.
4. The plaintiffs adduced 4 witnesses namely, PWs 1-4 and produced certain documents which were marked as Exhibit 1-10. On the other hand, the defendant's side adduced one witness namely, Md Rashedul Hossen as DW 1, who is the employee of the concerned Union Land Office. He has produce and proved attested Photocopy of BS Khatian No. 1 in which BS Plot No. 2510 and 2511 that arises out of SA Plot No. 772, have been recorded in the name of the Government.
5. The trial court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the evidence on record, by it's judgment and decree dated 8-8-2007 (decree signed on 12-8-2007), partly allowed the suit.
6. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial court, the Government has preferred Title Appeal No.104 of 2007, before the District Judge, Rajbari, which was heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Rajbari, who being the Appellate Court, has passed the impugned judgment and decree, allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court, vide it's judgment and decree dated 3-2-2011 (decree signed on 8-2-2011).
7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiffs-respondent-petitioners filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and obtained the present Rule.
8. Learned Advocates Mr Muhammad Jamiruddin Sircar, Mr Md Zahirul Islam with Mrs. Sahida Irin appeared for the petitioners. They, having placed the petition, along with the materials on record, mainly submits that, the plaintiffs have proved their case and that the property is originally belonged to Foyzuddin Sheikh and his name has been recorded in RS Khatian No. 771 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 772 of Mouza Uttor Uzanchar, PS Goalanda, District-Rajbari. They also submit that, the plaintiffs having filed and proved their respective title deeds in respect of their title which were duly marked as Exhibit Nos. 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 out of which Exhibit No. 9 is the bia deed filed in support of the title of Md Abdul Mozid and his wife Jorina Begum. They also submit that the plaintiffs have also filed and proved 8 sets of Khazzna Dakhilas in their names (Exhibit 3 series) and Municipality Tax receipts Exhibit 4. They further submit that, the PW Nos. 1, 2 and 4 have supported the case of the plaintiffs by corroborating each other whereas, the PW 3 Abdus Satter Sheikh, son of Foyzuddin Sheikh also supported the case of the plaintiffs. On the other hand, the DW 1 could not file any paper to show that the suit property was ever merged into the river Padma. Moreover, all the witnesses have supported the case of the plaintiffs that they were in possession and the DW 1, during his cross examination has admitted that, the river Padma was 5/6 KM far from the suit property and during tenure in the office, he has not seen any erosion for merging the suit property in the said river. Therefore, they submit, the appellate court ought to have dismissed the appeal and that the suit property belonged to the plaintiffs. But, the appellate court without at all considering the evidence on record as the last court of fact has allowed the appeal on technical ground that in schedule No. "Kha", the SA Khatian No. 172 is wrong. The learned Advocates further submit that, this is simply typing mistake, but they submit that the suit Plot No. 3206, lying at SA Khatian No. 772 (Exhibit 2) has been admitted by the defendant in its written statement. The appellate court, in passing the impugned judgment and decree, has failed to appreciate the facts and law involved in this case and thereby it has committed error of law resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Hence, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside and, therefore, this Rule has merit and the same may kindly be made absolute by decreeing the suit.
9. On the other hand, the learned DAG Mr Md Giasuddin Ahammad, Mr Md Shahabuddin Ahmed Tipu, AAG and Mr Md Shaifour Rahman Siddique, AAG, have appeared on behalf of the opposite party Government of Bangladesh. The learned DAG submits that, the trial court has found title in 7 decimals of land of plaintiff No. 4, however, the other plaintiffs did not file any appeal against the judgment of the trial court. Therefore, the appellate court in the absence of the other plaintiffs was not concerned and so far the plaintiff No. 4, in respect of 7 decimals of land was concerned. He next submits that, the suit property sold by Abdus Satter Sheikh son of Foyzuddin Sheikh is counted together with 38 decimals of land whereas, the plaintiffs claimed 41 decimals of land. Therefore, the plaint should have given boundary in as much as the property of the suit plot was not claimed by the plaintiffs. Therefore, the judgment and decree of the appellate court was absolutely correct and lawful and was based on evidence on record. Hence, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court may kindly be upheld and the Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged.
10. I have heard the learned Advocates for the petitioners, the learned DAG for the opposite party and also perused the application for revision, lower Court's record as well as the judgment of both the Courts below and other materials maintained in the lower court's record.
11. I am of the opinion that, the appellate court, as the last court of fact, ought to have assessed the evidence on record after framing the appropriate issues.
12. It is evident from the record that, in RS Khatian No. 771 of Mouza Uttor Uzanchar, name of Foyzuddin Sheikh has been recorded as co-sharer to the extent of 8 annas share as Riyot in total 1.40 acre of land and the suit Plot No. 3206 is also recorded in the SA Khatian No. 772. Similarly, in the said Mouza, 8 annas property has been recorded in the name of Foyzuddin Sheikh in total 1.40 decimals of land of this Khatain and that also records the suit Plot No. 3206.
13. On the other hand, in the written statement of the Government as well as the deposition of DW 1, has admitted that the BS Plot Nos. 2510 and 2511 have been recorded in BS Khatian No. 1 of the said Mouza has come from SA Khatian No. 772.
14. This being the admitted position, the court below ought to have found that, the suit property being RS/SA Plot No. 3206 belonged to Foyzuddin Sheikh, who is the predecessor of Abdus Satter Sheikh.
15. Besides, it is not disputed by any of the parties that Abdus Satter and his brother have inherited the suit property from their father, the recorded owner Foyzuddin Sheikh.
16. It is totally a different question as to whether the suit property was ever merged, or not, into the river Padam as claimed by the defendant.
17. The appellate court ought to have decided as to whether the plaintiffs have acquired good title and whether they were in possession of the suit property with reference to the exhibited documents and the issues of their possession of the suit property and as per the documents like Khazna Dakhalias. But, the issue has not been framed, nor has discussed.
18. The next issue is to be framed by the appellate court whether the property has been ever merged into river Padma which has not also been decided. The appellate court only has given focus on schedule "Kha" of the plaint, where apparently SA Khatian has been wrongly typed. Inspite of that, the plaintiffs had an opportunity to file an application in order to correct the schedule "Kha" of the plaint.
19. The last question is whether the appellate court can decide all these issues, including the issues of title and interest of the respondents, who did not prefer any appeal. The provisions of Order 41, rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure are relevant to answer this, which reads as follows:—
Rule 33.—The Appellate Court shall have power to pass any decree and make any order which ought to have been passed or made and to pass or make such further or other decree or order as the case may require, and this power may be exercised by the Court notwithstanding that the appeal is as to part only of the decree and may be exercised in favour of all or any of the respondents or parties, although such respondents or parties may not have filed any appeal or objection.
<u>20. Therefore, the law is clear that, the appellate court has power to decide the case as a whole, although the appeal has been preferred only against part of the decree or by some of the parties. This power can, however, be exercised to settle the rights and title of all the parties to the suit, even though some of them had not preferred an appeal or cross-objection, inspite of having scope for the same. In other words, entire decree is liable to be judicially scrutinized by the appellate court, in the light of the pleadings and the evidence led before the trial court, since an appeal is continuation of the original suit.</u>
21. The question as to whether giving no boundary of the schedule "Kha" was fatal in this case. The plaintiffs have claimed the entire 41 decimals of land of SA Plot No. 3206 of Mouza Uttor Uzanchar, PS Goalnanda, District-Rajbari.
22. If the plaintiffs claim 41 decimals of land of Plot No. 3206, then boundary was not necessary, but even if a small portion is left then the boundary will be required, but that can be corrected at any stage.
23. Considering all the facts and circumstance, I am of the opinion that, the title of Foyzuddin Sheikh in RS/SA Plot No. 3206 has been clearly proved by the evidence on record. However, the appellate court, as the last court of fact, had power to decide the case in its entirety in view of the provisions of law discussed above and in the light of the oral and documentary evidence on record placed before the trial court. As such, I find that this is a fit case to send back to the appellate court on remand so that the parties can rectify the errors.
24. The learned Advocate for the petitioner during his submission pointed out that, they have purchased 2 decimals of land from Abdus Satter Sheikh, in the suit Plot and the plaintiffs were in possession of entire 41 decimals of the suit property, though, inadvertently omitted in the plaint.
25. In view of the foregoing discussions, I sent back the case to the appellate court to frame necessary issues and to decide as to whether Foyzuddin Sheikh was the owner of entire 41 decimals of land, recorded in SA/RS Plot No. 3206. The appellate court is further, directed to frame issue as to whether the plaintiffs have derived any title in the suit property by virtue of the documents placed and proved before the trial court. Besides, the appellate court should also decide as to whether the suit property was ever merged into the river Padma and it should record its decision and to take additional evidence, if necessary.
26. With the observations, made above, this Rule should be disposed of.
Order
In the result, the Rule is disposed of.
The impugned judgment and decree dated 3-2-2011 (decree signed on 8-2-2011), passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Rajbari, in Title Appeal No.104 of 2007, allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 8-8-2007 (decree signed on 12-8-2007), passed by the Assistant Judge (In charge), Goalanda, Rajbari, in Title Suit No. 33 of 2006, is hereby set-aside.
The case is sent back on remand to the appellate court to frame and decide the following issues, in the light of the observation made above, namely, (1) whether Foyzuddin Sheikh was the owner of entire 41 decimals of land, recorded in SA/RS Plot No. 3206,
(2) whether the plaintiffs have derived title in the suit property by virtue of the documents placed and proved before the trial court,
(3) whether the suit property was ever merged into the river Padma and it should record its decision and may take additional evidence, if necessary.
The order of status-quo granted earlier by this court is hereby vacated.
No order as to cost.
Let a copy of this judgment along with the LCR be sent to the concerned Court at once.
End.

full_judgment:
Md Ali Reza, J: The petitioners in this writ petition obtained Rule Nisi against the impugned order dated 25-7-2022 স্মারক নং উভূঅ/শ্রী/গাজী/বিবিধ ১১৯/২২ passed by respondent 4 in Miscellaneous Case 119 of 2022 correcting the RS khatian 213 and RS plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701 in violation of circular vide Memo No. 31.00.0000.042.67.031.11(Part-1)-343 published by Gazette notification dated 29-7-2021 (Annexure-G) should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. At the time of issuance of the Rule the impugned order was stayed for a period of 3(three) months which was subsequently extended and is still in force.
2. The case of the petitioners is that Abdul Mozid, Abdul Aziz, Abdul Gofur and Abdul Johor are owners of 1.98 acres of land of RS plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701 appertaining to RS khatian 213 of Mouza Telihati of Upazila Shreepur. One Shamsul Haq Master who was the predecessor of petitioners 1-3 purchased 0.86 acres from the RS tenants and had been in possession upon mutation and payment of rent from the year 2008. One Abdullah Al Baki also purchased 0.91 acres and mutated his name. Due to illness he executed a power of attorney on 15-6-2022 in favour of petitioner 4. Meanwhile one Sultan Mia and others filed Title Suit 365 of 2019 for declaration of title and recovery of possession and also for partition on 15-9-2019 in respect of 1.98 acres out of 5.70 acres in which petitioner 1 and predecessor of petitioner 4 being defendants 1 and 2 respectively filed written statement on 24-2-2021. In the suit plaintiffs' application for injunction was rejected on 20-3-2022 for want of prima facie case and they along with others filed Miscellaneous Case 119 of 2022 before Assistant Commissioner (Land) Sreepur for correction of RS record 213 on 12-4-2022 on ground of clerical mistake due to wrong entry of the names of the tenants. Assistant Commissioner (Land) who is respondent 4 passed the impugned order on 25-7-2022 in violation of circular published in Additional Gazette on 29-7-2021 and the RS khatian was changed very unfairly in favour of third party on 20-11-2022. Thereafter the plaintiffs of the suit and one Asaduzzaman filed Review Case 60 of 2022 in which predecessors of petitioners 1 and 4 were parties and they for the first time came to know about the proceeding on 21-12-2022 and they also filed two review petitions on 11-1-2023 and 23-1-2023 for setting aside the impugned order dated 25-7-2022. In Review Case 60 of 2022 they filed application for stay all further proceedings of that review case with reference to Title Suit 365 of 2019 now renumbered as 417 of 2021 but respondent 4 did not pay any heed to it. Petitioners 1-3 in the meantime filed an application for their addition in Review Case 60 of 2022 but that was rejected by respondent 4. Respondent 4 had no jurisdiction to pass such impugned order. Respondent 4 exceeded jurisdiction vested upon it and the impugned order dated 25-7-2022 is ultra vires being passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
3. Respondents 6-8 filed an application for their addition in the writ petition which was allowed on 9-8-2023.
4. Added respondents 6-8 filed affidavit-in-opposition and contested the Rule. The case of the added respondents 6-8 is that CS tenant Mohim Sheikh transferred 2.20 acres in favour of his wife Moymon Nesa and SA khatian 777 was correctly prepared in her name but RS khatian 213 was mistakenly prepared in the names of the transferors of the petitioners in respect of RS plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701. The successors to Moymon Nesa later on appointed Nurul Islam as their attorney who got ex-parte decree of declaration of title and partition in Title Suit 221 of 2010 and entered into a contract for sale with respondent 7 on 9-8-2010 and in furtherance of the same kabala was registered in favour of respondents 6-8 on 10-1-2022. These respondents along with Asaduzzaman and 17 others had no knowledge about the writ petition and this writ petition suffers defect of party and since the writ petitioners have already filed review against the impugned order this Rule Nisi is liable to be discharged being not maintainable because of availing the statutory remedy.
5. Mr Ragib Rouf Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that respondent 4 had no jurisdiction to pass the impugned order according to clause 7Ua) provided in circular dated 29-7-2021 and the impugned order has been passed by committing jurisdictional error and the same is liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. He also submits that respondent 4 has exceeded power vested upon and he had to wait till Title Suit 365 of 2022 meets its finality. Respondent 4 has stepped out of jurisdiction by acting unreasonably and capriciously in disregard of public policy and neglected and misinterpreted the Rules framed in memo dated 29-7-2021. Respondent 4 misdirected in law by adopting a wrong approach in passing the impugned order and the same being done without lawful authority is liable to be set-aside.
6. On the other hand Mr Faysal Hasan Arif, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of added respondents 6-7 submits that the instant writ petition was filed with a malafide intention to obtain order from this Court as Mr Asaduzzaman and 17 others as well as these respondents despite being necessary parties were not made parties and this Rule Nisi is not maintainable for defect of party. He further submits that the writ petitioners have filed review application before respondent 4 against the impugned order which is still pending thus they are not entitled to have any remedy in writ jurisdiction. He strongly submits that the writ petition is not maintainable because petitioners did not produce the judgment and order dated 25-7-2022 without which the impugned order whether was passed illegally cannot be adjudged and the clerical mistake in khatian which has been corrected was done upon proper exercise of jurisdictional power with lawful authority and the Rule Nisi having no merit is liable to be discharged.
7. We have heard the learned Advocates of respective parties and perused the writ petition and the affidavit-in-opposition with annexures appended thereto.
8. The petitioners claim to be transferees from RS tenants and respondents 6-8 claim through transfers from heir of CS tenant but exact detail of title of neither party is available to the satisfaction of the Court. Both parties claim 1.98 acres of land from RS plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701 of RS record 213. From perusal of annexure-D it appears that one Sultan Mia and others filed Title Suit 365 of 2019 on 15-9-2019 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Gazipur for declaration of title and recovery of possession with partition which is now renumbered as Title Suit 417 of 2021 and pending in the Court of Second Senior Assistant Judge, Gazipur in which present petitioner 1 and predecessor of petitioner 4 as defendants 1 and 2 respectively filed written statement on 24-2-2021. From reading of annexure-E it further appears that in that suit plaintiffs' prayer for injunction was refused on 20-3-2022 on the finding that they have no prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in their favour and there remains no possibility of suffering irreparable loss. Respondents did not challenge or deny this statement of fact introducing this suit. After failing in injunction Sultan and others filed the disputed Miscellaneous Case 119 of 2022 on 12-4-2022 before respondent 4. It is evident from annexure-F that Sultan Mia and others are successive heirs of Moymona from whom respondents 6-8 also claim. Petitioners claim through opposite parties 1-4 to the miscellaneous case who are RS tenants as is Moymona. So question of defect of party loses its importance considering the fact of the present case and laws relating thereto. The main question is to look into as to whether the impugned order dated 25-7-2022 is ultra vires being passed without jurisdiction.
<u>9. It transpires from RS record 213 (Annexure-A) that Moymona who was the predecessor and previous owner of both Sultan Mia and others as well as respondents 6-8 has got share in 1.96 acres in RS plot 2596 and on the other side the previous owners of the petitioners were RS tenants Gofur, Johur, Aziz, Mozid in respect of 1.98 acres of land with different shares in different RS plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701. The miscellaneous case was filed for correction of clerical mistake happened in RS record 213 to replace the name of Moymona in place of Gofur and others with reference to annexure-J dated 29-7-2021 which is a circular published in Additional Gazette. The petitioners of the miscellaneous case want to have Moymona's name appearing in column of plot 2576 exchanged with the names of Gofur and others whose different and definite shares have been recorded in plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701 and accordingly the impugned order was passed. This case falls under section 143 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with Rule 23(3) of Tenancy Rules, 1955 along with circular published in additional Gazette on 29-7-2021 (Annexure-J). This circular concerns with the clerical mistake in the khatian and deals with such correction under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with Rule 23(3) of Tenancy Rules 1955 after serving section 144 to completion. The object of the circular is that the officers empowered and responsible under the law and rules cannot in some cases give the remedy sought by the people to correct the khatian prepared and finally published in the latest survey as they do not have a clear understanding of the purpose of law and this circular aims at giving a clear idea to the officers to properly follow the instructions of the procedure of the provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Tenancy Rules regarding correction of clerical errors in the khatian. Rule 23(3) of the Tenancy Rules 1955 has been referred to in Clause 3 and clerical mistake is defined in Clause 4 of the circular which shows that a clerical error is an error which is believed to have been made in good faith by mistake or by carelessness and which does not involve the proprietary interest of another person and which if rectified would not impair the interest of another person or diminish or increase the amount of the land. Clause 7 provides mode of correction and sub-clause J is relevant here what says that if in correcting the clerical error in the khatian the ownership is affected to the effect that the amount of the property is reduced or increased and the ownership of another is changed or someone else is benefited or harmed then the revenue officer will have no jurisdiction to correct the khatian and it will be treated as a civil dispute and the action of the Assistant Commissioner will be excluded. The provisions of this circular are very reasonable and equitable and also lawful in the interest of the people and in support of the original law.</u>
10. As discussed above about the fact and law and from a combined reading of the schedule of Annexure-F and Annexure-G it transpires that the impugned order brought about a change in the extent of the land which was beyond the jurisdiction of the revenue officer and which was only cognizable in the civil Court. The revenue Court is not a civil Court and the revenue officer had no right or jurisdiction to pass the impugned order. It also appears from the record that there are several civil suits pending in respect of the land in dispute which is not denied by respective parties. The order is apparently illegal and ultra vires being passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Respondent 4 had no jurisdiction to pass the impugned order.
11. We therefore find merit in this Rule and accordingly the rule is made absolute. The impugned order is set-aside. The ad interim order passed by this Court stands vacated.
Communicate this judgment to the concern.
End.
