full_judgment:
Md Ali Reza, J: This appeal at the instance of defendants 1-6 is directed against judgment and decree dated 3-6-2008 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Jhalakati in Title Suit 05 of 2004 decreeing the suit in part.
2. Respondents as plaintiffs filed Title Suit 05 of 2004 on 19-6-2004 for partition and for further declaration that the judgment and decree dated 4-4-1985 and its correction order dated 4-3-2007 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Court No. 1, Jhalakati in Title Suit 126 of 1983 is fraudulent, collusive, null and void and not binding upon-the plaintiffs.
3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that A. Gofur was tenant under Ray Bihari Lal Bahadur represented by Administrator General of Bengal. Due to arrear of rent landlord filed Rent Suit 1941 of 1940 and got decree and the suit land was sold in Rent Execution Case 622 of 1943 and auction was purchased by Hachen Uddin on 9-11- 1943 and got possession on 14-3-1944. It is further stated that another Rent Suit 1927 of 1948 was subsequently filed and the suit land was again sold in Rent Execution Case 404 of 1949 and auction was purchased by Gogon Ali and Mofizuddin Howlader on 31-5-1949 which was confirmed on 14-4-1949 and later on possession was delivered. Auction purchasers settled the suit land with the predecessors of the plaintiffs named Rahman Faraji, Kader Faraji, Abdul Hakim, Gani Faraji, Abdul Motaleb, Abdul Khaleque, Muslemuddin and Tofayel Ahmed at an annual rental of 50 taka 6 anna and accordingly RS record 487 was prepared in their names. Gani, Motaleb, Khaleque possessed 8 annas share wherefrom they sold 0.304 acres to plaintiff 1 and Erfan by kabala dated 24-3-1955. Erfan sold 0.16 acres to plaintiff 4 and 0.16 acres to plaintiff 2 and 3 by two kabalas dated 21-4-1983. Rahman executed a patta in respect of 0.32 acres of land on 5-6-1950 to Mofizuddin who sold the same to Erfan, Hachen, Azhar by kabala dated 3-4-1956. Erfan transferred his share to plaintiffs 2 and 3. Azhar made an oral gift of his share to grandson plaintiff 2. It is also stated that one Tofazzal sold by kabala dated 12-4-1949 to Ibrahim who sold 0.63 acres to Erfan and plaintiff 1 through kabala dated 14-11-1955. Erfan orally gifted his share to plaintiff 2. Tofayel transferred 0.81 acres of land in favour of Sultan, Lehaj Uddin, Anwara through kabala 2976 dated 23-10-1956. Sultan died leaving behind plaintiffs 10, 11 and 12. Lehaj Uddin was the predecessor of plaintiffs 13-18. Anwara died and her heirs sold the land to plaintiff 2. Tofayel also sold 0.32 acres to plaintiff 1 through kabala dated 7-3-1955. Plaintiff 1 sold 0.08 acres to plaintiff 20 on 12-6-2007. Thus plaintiffs acquired 5.44 acres of land as mentioned in schedule `Kha'. The RS and SA record were correctly prepared jointly with the predecessor of the defendants. Due to inconvenience in possession plaintiff asked defendants for partition but they did not pay any heed to it and refused the same on 2nd Boishakh, 1411 BS. Hence the suit was filed.
4. Defendants 1-6 appeared and contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all material statements made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit is barred by limitation and also under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It was further stated that Rashid, Hachen, Tachen, Samed, Rafizuddin, Atabar were owners in possession and they settled 9.77 acres of land at a yearly rental of 50 taka 6 anna to Abdur Rahman Faraji by registered dakhila dated 1-3-1946 but his brothers' names were wrongly inserted in RS khatian 487 along with his name. Rahman died leaving behind daughter Kulsum, wives Shamsunnessa and Rahima, sons defendants 1-6 named Rob, Sobhan, Huq, Wahid, Barek, Awal. Sons and mothers filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 on 26-4-1978 for declaration of title against the wrong record. Suit was renumbered as 389 of 1981 and 126 of 1983. Defendants 6(Ka)/6(Ga)/15-17/18(Ka)-18(Kha) /20(Ka) and plaintiffs filed compromise petition in the suit and accordingly suit was decreed on 4-4-1985 and title of Rahman's heirs was declared. Later on defendant 12 of that suit named Fulboru filed Miscellaneous Case 34 of 1985 which was allowed on 30-7-1988. Present defendants then preferred Civil Revision 186 of 1988 in the then Barishal Bench of this Division which was transferred to Dhaka High Court and renumbered as Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Sufia is the wife of Lehaj Uddin and mother of present plaintiffs 13-18. She died and her heirs executed a deed of relinquishment on 5-5-1991 and admitted title of the present defendants. Accordingly parties entered into compromise on 5-3-1998 which was allowed and the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 remained intact and the Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998. The case of the plaintiffs is false. Predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 named Hachen also registered a nadabi dated 5-6-1995 admitting the title and possession of the present defendants. Hachen Ali is still alive. Meanwhile present defendants filed GR Case 31 of 1998 in which the statement of Title Suit 126 of 1983 was given. Earlier Hachen filed Miscellaneous Petition Case 213 of 1991 in which possession was found in favour of these appellant-defendants. Plaintiffs have definite knowledge of earlier Title Suit 126 of 1983. Present defendants have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land by living in their homestead and through cultivation upon payment of rent. Son of plaintiff 3 recently purchased from the defendants on 1-4-2003 admitting the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983. The suit being false is liable to be dismissed with cost.
5. The Joint District Judge framed as many as 06(six) issues as to maintainability, defect of party, hotch potch, whether plaintiffs have title and possession in the suit land, whether the judgment dated 4-4-1985 and decree dated 9-4-1985 passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Jhalakati are binding upon the plaintiffs, whe they plaintiffs can get the relief as prayed for.
6. In course of trial plaintiffs examined 03(three) witnesses whereas defendants examined one and both the parties adduced documentary evidence in order to prove their respective cases.
7. The Joint District Judge decreed the suit in part by judgment and decree dated 3-6-2008 on the finding that defendants could not offer satisfactory answer against the correctness of record of rights and records were correctly prepared and plaintiffs have acquired 3.92 acres of land through transfers and the nadabi document as claimed by defendants do not confer title and DW 1 admitted that there is only one plaintiff who was party to earlier suit thus the impugned decree is not binding upon the rest 19 plaintiffs and since plaintiffs have title in the instant suit land the decree of Title Suit 126 of 1983 passed in favour of defendants becomes inoperative.
8. Defendants being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment have preferred the instant appeal. Plaintiffs however did not file any cross appeal for the rest 1.52 acres of land.
9. Mr Swapon Kumar Dutta, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the plaintiffs did not make out any case as to why the decree of `Ga' schedule is fraudulent and not binding upon them and plaintiffs cannot escape from discharging such heavy onus which squarely lies upon them. RS record was wrongly prepared in the names of all sons of Sonamuddi Faraji for which settlement holder Rahman's heirs filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 renumbered as 126 of 1983 for declaration of title against such wrong record impleading other sons of Sonamuddi or their heirs and got their title declared which was affirmed by this Division in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 on 25-3-1998. That judgment was not challenged and examined by our Appellate Division and this suit was filed after 06(six) years on 19-6-2004. On the strength of such decree defendants have mutated their names and have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land upon payment of rent. Plaintiffs are never their co-sharers and this suit being false is liable to be dismissed outright. He further submits that the deeds of relinquishment executed by the then defendants in the suit and revision although do not confer title but those are strong admissions and the present plaintiffs are now estopped from denying the title of the appellants. He then submits that Title Suit 126 of 1983 was mentioned in Criminal PS Case 04 of 1986 and after a long lapse of time the instant suit for declaration against the 'Ga' schedule decree dated 4-4-1985 is barred by limitation. He then referring to `Ga' schedule decree strongly submits that the heirs of some of the defendants of earlier suit along with others filed the instant suit thus this suit suffers multifariousness because parties to earlier suit although does not require declaration of title but the rest requires such relief thus their claim is vague and suit cannot run in accordance with law. In furtherance of such submission he proceeds that the rest defendants of earlier suit who did not file the instant suit must be made defendants to protect their valuable rights but the same having been not done the instant suit suffers defect of party. He finally submits that the Joint District Judge misquoted the evidence of DW 1 and arrived at a wrong conclusion. In support of his submission he refers the cases of Subitri Bari vs Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property and other; 39 DLR 172; Rezaul Karim and others vs Shamsuzzoha and others, 49 DLR (AD) 68; Abu Naser Mohd. Wahidun Nabi and another vs Balai Roy and others, 10 MLR (AD) 121; Akitullah and others vs Zafala Begum and others, 54 DLR (AD) 74 and prays for allowing the appeal.
10. Mr Sarder Abul Hossain, learned Advocate on the other hand appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the Joint District Judge upon proper appreciation of evidence has rightly passed the judgment. He draws our attention to RS record 487 and submits that the RS record has got its presumptive value and defendants could not dislodge such presumption by any convincing evidence. The Joint District Judge upon perusal of Exhibits-3-9 has correctly found that the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree in part which may not be interfered with by this Court. The claim of the defendants relying upon two nadabi documents does not deserve any consideration because those do not confer any title. He laid much emphasis on the statement of DW 1 made in cross and submits that according to the admission of DW 1 the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 is not binding upon the plaintiffs and plaintiffs have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land. He referring to the deposition of DW 1 submits that the Joint District Judge has passed the judgment upon due consideration of materials on record and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. In course of hearing Mr Hossain filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 15-3-2023 and on 30-3-2023 filed another application for production of additional evidence. In support of those applications he submits that at the time of hearing of this appeal plaintiffs have come to know some important facts and documents with regard to their title which are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the dispute and unless those are considered and allowed the respondents shall suffer irreparable loss and injury.
11. We have heard the learned Advocates and examined all the materials on record and also gone through the impugned judgment as well as the grounds taken in appeal.
12. From reading of paragraph 2 of the plaint it appears that plaintiffs cited two auction issues. First auction was purchased by Hachen Uddin and the second one was by Gogon Ali and Mafizuddin. Plaintiffs claim their title through settlement from Gogon and Mafizuddin on the other hand defendants claim their title through settlement from Hachen Talukder and others. Plaintiffs claim that according to the settlement RS record 487 Exhibit-IX was correctly prepared in the names of six sons of Sonamuddi Faraji named Rahman, Kader, Hakim, Gani, Motaleb, Khaleque Rahman is the predecessor of contesting defendants 1-6. Plaintiffs did not produce any document of title showing settlement in their favour nor did they bother to mention the date of taking such settlement. Plaintiffs also did not produce the suit registers of those two rent suits despite availability of such documents in the concerned office. From reading of Exhibits-Kha and Kha(1) which are judgment and decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 it appears that the dispute arose in 1978 when defendants filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit 126 of 1983 for declaration of title against wrong entry in RS khatian 487 Exhibit-IX. In that suit the present defendants were plaintiffs and claimed that their father Rahman took settlement from Hachen and others by a registered dakhila dated 1-3-1946 Exhibit-Ka at an annual rental of 50 taka 6 anna but Rahman's brother named Gani managed to procure such wrong- record Exhibit-IX in collusion with the survey employees by dishonest means and out of greed. That suit was decreed on compromise against defendants 6(Ka)- 6(Ga)/15-17/18(Ka)-18(Gha)/20(Ka) and ex-parte against the rest. Defendants 15-18 of the earlier suit are RS tenants and consenting parties. The non-contesting defendant 12 named Fulbaru filed. Miscellaneous Case 34 of 1985 which was allowed on 30-7-1988. Present defendants filed Civil Revision 186 of 1988 which was subsequently renumbered as Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 wherein the heirs of deceased defendant 13 Lehajuddin executed a registered deed of relinquishment on 5-5-1991 Exhibit-Uma and admitted the title of the present defendants. The heirs of deceased Lehajuddin are plaintiffs 13-18 in this suit. Hachen who is the predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 also admitted title and possession of the present defendants and executed a deed of relinquishment dated 5-6-1995 Exhibit-Cha. Subsequently heirs of deceased Fulbaru filed compromise with present defendants and admitted their title and possession in the suit land and accordingly Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998 in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 as apparent from Exhibits-Ga and Gha. Furthermore present defendants ailed GR Case 31 of 1998 in which the statement of Title Suit 126 of 1983 was given and the order sheet of GR Case is Exhibit-Chha. There is no reason to believe that the present plaintiffs had no knowledge of the earlier Title Suit 126 of 1983.
13. There are three aspects important here to be considered. First is the judgment and order dated 25-3-1998 passed in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 wherein the judgment and decree dated 9-4-1985 passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 was maintained with regard to the same land but no one challenged that judgment and order passed in revision in the Honourable Appellate Division. Plaintiffs did not make out any case of fraud, forgery, collusion et cetera against Exhibits- Kha series, Ga and Gha. This suit is barred under Order 6, rules 2 and 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Plaint should contain material facts which constitute the cause of action. All primary facts which must be proved to establish the existence of the cause of action are material facts. Decree has been challenged in this case but it is very surprising to us that no single word has been spelt out against the decree mentioned in schedule-Ga to the plaint. There is no reason to go against such a decree being passed by a competent Court of law and affirmed by the High Court Division. We cannot sit over the judgment passed by this Court except any allegation of fraud. The cause of action of the instant case is apparently false.
14. Second is the question of limitation. The `Ga' schedule decree was challenged after 19(nineteen) years. The judgment and decree was passed in Title Suit 126 of 1986 on 9-4-1985 Exhibit-'Kha series'. The instant suit challenging that decree was filed on 19-6-2004. The judgment of Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 was passed on 25-3-1998 Exhibits-Ga and Gha. There is sufficient and satisfactory evidence available in the instant case to decide the question of limitation although no issue on such point was framed by the trial Court despite its legal inevitability and necessity in order to reach to a satisfactory conclusion. This Court finds no reason to send the suit down on remand for framing an issue on question of limitation thereby shirk its responsibility. This Court has ample co-extensive power as like as the trial Court to question whether the suit is barred by limitation by framing an issue naming the same as issue No. 7 and disposing of the same under Section 107(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure when sufficient evidence are obtainable from the record to the satisfaction of the Court. The predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 and 13-18 were defendants in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and they executed two deeds of relinquishment dated 5-6-1995 Exhibit-Cha and 5-5-1991 Exhibit-Uma and according to compromise the Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998 and both Exhibits-Uma and Cha remained unchallenged in the instant suit although the executants are the plaintiffs in the suit. Thus it evidently transpires to us that plaintiffs have every knowledge of Exhibit-Kha series with Ga and Gha but they have challenged the decree after the statutory period of time. If it were argued that knowledge of some of the plaintiffs is not the knowledge of others in that case the suit fails on ground of multifariousness. Therefore issue No. 7 as framed by this Court goes against the case of the plaintiffs.
15. Third is that the suit was decreed in part relying on the denial part of DW 1. We paid our keen attention and went through the entire deposition of DW 1. From reading of the decree of Title Suit 126 of 1983 Exhibit-Kha(1) it is apparent that present plaintiffs 5, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 along with others were defendants in Title Suit 126 of 1983. Thus it appears that while recording the deposition of DW 1 the word "not a fact" was mistakenly omitted from some places at the time of taking denial part by the presiding Judge. It becomes evidently clear when DW 1 immediately denied the suggestion at the end of his deposition as he stated that it was not a fact that plaintiffs possessed the suit land. Thus the finding of the Joint District Judge that since DW 1 admitted that there was only one defendant who is now the plaintiff and since the other plaintiffs were not parties the decree is not binding is abjectly perverse and misconceived and against documentary evidence. The lower Court failed to apply its judicial mind and did not even notice Exhibit-Kha(1) showing names and numbers of defendants of Title Suit 126 of 1983 and compare the same with the present plaint. The lower Court also went against the settled principle of law that plaintiff has to prove his own case independent of defence weakness.
16. Now we are going to consider the title of the parties. Plaintiff 14 who was one of the executants of Exhibit-Uma dated 5-5-1991 has deposed as PW 1. Although Exhibit-Uma is a deed of relinquishment and the same does not confer title but it is a registered document of admission and since no relief was prayed against Exhibits-Uma and Cha the documents stand good and plaintiff 14 is bound by such admission made in Exhibit-Uma and he is estopped from denying such admission thus the value of his testimony is greatly diminished. PW 2 and PW 3 deposed on possession and PW 3 failed to corroborate PW 2 as he admitted in cross that the land of Abdur Rahman is enjoyed by his sons. However since this is mainly a suit for partition evidence on possession does not carry much value except title. Plaintiffs claim title through settlement from auction purchasers Gogon and Mofijuddin. But they did not file any document of such settlement. It was not also explained away by them as to why they could not put forth such document. The document of title of the defendants for the selfsame land has been validated in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Defendants claim title through settlement from Hachen and others by registered dakhila Exhibit-Ka dated 1-3-1946. It appears from the pleadings and evidence that plaintiffs have relied on RS record 487 Exhibit-IX as the basis of their claim. Record of right is not a document of title. Moreover this Exhibit-IX has lost its value' by virtue of the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and the judgment passed by this Division in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Defendants on the strength of decree mutated their names by Exhibit-Jha series and have been maintaining possession upon payment of rent Exhibit-Jha series. Earlier respondents filed three applications for amendment of the plaint and for taking additional evidence along with a supplementary affidavit but according to the order dated 30-11-2017 passed by a bench of this Court respondents did not press those applications at the time of hearing. So those applications are rejected being not pressed. Respondents also filed another application for amendment of the plaint on 15-3-2023 and also for acceptance of additional evidence on 30-3-2023 and those applications were heard. In the amendment of plaint respondents have made out a new case of kabuliyat and dakhila and in its support filed certified copies of kabuliyat and dakhila through application for acceptance of additional evidence. We have carefully examined those two documents and it appears that the kabuliyat dated 17-8-1944 was accepted by Hachen and others and they granted a dakhila on the same day to Rahman and his brothers. The second auction as drawn in the original plaint has been disowned in this amendment. Earlier plaintiffs claimed through Gogon and Mofijuddin and the rent was 50 taka 6 anna and quantum of the holding was 9.72 acres according to schedule-Ka. Now they are claiming through Hachen and others and the joma is 44 taka 8 anna and quantum of joma is 8.75 acres which is inconsistent with schedule-Ka. The dakhila shows that education cess is fixed at 2 taka 4 anna which actually was not imposed at the time in 1351 BS as found our Appellate Division in the case of Joynal Abedin Molla vs Aliyar Rahman and others, 1983 BLD (AD) 105. Plaintiffs were acquainted with Exhibit-Ka dated 1-3-1946 since 1978 when Title Suit 166 of 1978 renumbered as Title Suit 126 of 1983 was filed. That document stands good in the suit and revision Exhibit-Kha series, Ga and Gha. Now after around 26(twenty-six) years plaintiffs have come forward with those applications in view to fill up their lacuna by making out a new case on their acquisition of title to the surprise of the other party. The other party cannot be taken by surprise specially when a valuable right is accrued in their favour by lapse of time. Had Exhibit-Kha series been found fraudulent according to pleading and evidence in that case these proposed applications would have been taken in adjudication. It also calls for our attention that in Title Suit 126 of 1983 the RS tenants Gani Faraji, Abul Khaleque, Tofayel Ahmed admitting the title of Rahman Faraji which he acquired through Exhibit-Ka entered into compromise which was not denied in revision Exhibits-Ga and Gha. Court has to follow the principles of law and we have no option but to reject those applications filed after such a belated stage. It has also come to our notice that in paragraph 2 of the application for production of additional evidence it is admitted that the original kabulyat was under the custody of executant Abdur Rahman Faraji thus it appears that the same was not acted upon being not accepted by the landlord.
<u>17. Khaleque, Gani, Motaleb claiming through settlment from the so-called auction purchasers Gogon and Mofijuddin sold 0.304 acres to plaintiff 1 and Erfan by kabala dated 24-3-1955 Exhibit-3. Schedule-2 of this document shows that 1112 decimals of land situated in Rajapur was shown to have been sold but plaint does not show any land belonging to them in Rajapur and document was also registered in Rajapur Sub-registry office instead of Kathaliya. Erfan being one of the transferees of Exhibit-3 sold 0.32 acres which is more than his share to plaintiffs 2, 3, 4 by two documents dated 21-4-1983 Exhibits-4 and 5. Plaint does not say anything about Exhibit-6. The transferee of Exhibit-7 made an oral gift to plaintiff 2 but no evidence was led in its support. One of the transferees of Exhibit-8 named Lehajuddin was the predecessor of defendants 13(Ka)-13(Da) in Title Suit 126 of 1983 who are now plaintiffs 13-18 and executants of Exhibit-Uma. The identity and claim of the plaintiffs are so inconsistent that there is no way to make any sense out of it. As discussed above the basis of plaintiffs' title is unfounded and this suit cannot be decreed without ascertaining title first. Without a definite case of declaration of title this suit for partition simpliciter is not at all maintainable specially when Exhibit-Kha series along with Ga and Gha stand against plaintiffs' title as a bar and those have never been confronted. Those are unanswered and kept untouched. Plaintiffs have failed to prove their case and the present suit is barred by limitation as discussed above.</u>
18. The lower Court found that defendants could not make any satisfactory reply against the SA record. He did not even bother to notice the SA and RS record distinctively. Court failed to appreciate that the satisfactory reply against the record of right was Exhibits-Ka and Kha series along with Ga and Gha. The Court abruptly found the SA and RS record are correct without assigning any reason and also miscalculated the quantum of land of 3.92 acres in granting the part decree without showing any reason as to why the remaining land could not be given. The lower Court misconceived the law and facts of the case and arrived at a wrong conclusion. Plaintiffs have failed to prove their own case and it appears that plaintiffs out of greed have filed this suit if the land or portion of it could be consumed in any way. They did not file any cross appeal for the rest 1.52 acres. The claim of the plaintiffs is absolutely false.
19. We are of the view that plaintiffs are not entitled to any decree and judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is set-aside and the appeal is allowed. There will be no order as to costs.
Communicate this judgment and send down the lower Court's record.
End.

parties:
Ayub Ali (Md) and others   Petitioners
VS
Bangladesh and others   Respondents
full_judgment:
Zafar Ahmed, J: In the instant writ petition, the petitioners prayed for absorption/regularization of their services or making the same permanent into the regular set up of the respondent No.2 Dhaka North City Corporation.
2. This Court, on 4-12-2018, issued a Rule Nisi.
3. The respondent No. 2 contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition.
4. The relevant facts, in brief, are that following recruitment notices published in the daily newspapers in 2010 and 2011 for recruitment of heavy vehicle driver-cum-cleaner, truck cleaner and heavy vehicle driver temporarily on daily `no work to pay' basis (muster roll) the petitioners were appointed in the respective posts in 2011 in the then. Dhaka City Corporation, now Dhaka North City Corporation. It was categorically stated in the appointment letters that the appointment was temporary and it was based on muster roll 'no work no pay'. Since the appointment, the petitioners have been working in the respective posts as per terms and conditions of the appointment letters. Now, they claim absorption/regularization of their services or making their services permanent. The appointments were made according to the provision of section 67 of the স্থানীয় সরকার (সিটি কর্পোরেশন) আইন, ২০০৯ which states, -এর বিধান অনুসারে নিয়োগগুলি করা হয়েছিল, যেখানে বলা হয়েছে, "কর্পোরেশন, বরাদ্দ সাপেক্ষে এবং ক্ষমতা পূর্বমোদন অনুসারে, তাৎক্ষণিক কোন জরুরী কার্য সম্পাদনের জন্য মীর বীর সদস্য নিয়োজিত করতে পারি”. Having been aware of the terms and conditions of the appointment letters and the relevant law, the petitioners joined in the service of the respondent No.2. No promise was made by the concerned authority that the services of the petitioners would be made permanent or that their services would be absorbed/regularized into the regular set up of the respondent No. 2.
5. The issue as to absorption and regularization of employees of development projects and daily basis/casual workers has been finally laid to rest by the apex Court in Secretary, Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock vs Abdul Razzak, 71 DLR (AD) 395 and in The Director-General, Bangladesh Rural Development Board (BRDB), Dhaka vs Asma Sharif, 72 DLR (AD) 188.
6. In the case reported in 71 DLR (AD) 395, it was held—
"A person who bases his claim, on the doctrine of legitimate expectation, in the first instance, must satisfy that there is a foundation, that is, he has locus standi to make such claim. Such claim has to be determined not according to the claimant's perception but in the public interest".
7. It was further held in 71 DLR (AD) 395 that,
"No court can direct the Government or its instrumentalities to regularize the service of the officers and employees of the development project in the revenue budget in the cases where statutory requirements have not been fulfilled. Regularization cannot be claimed as a matter of right. It is statutory requirement that opportunity shall be given to eligible persons by public notification and recruitment should be according to the valid procedure and appointment should be of the qualified persons found fit for appointments to a post or an office under the Government. When the High Court Division is pproached for relief by filing writ petition, necessarily the High Court Division has to ask itself whether the person before it had any legal right to be enforced or not. It cannot be directed to devise a third mode of selection.
8. Accordingly, it is observed that:
1. The legitimate expectation would not override the statutory provision. The doctrine of legitimate expectation cannot be invoked for creation of posts to facilitate absorption in the offices of the regular cadres/non cadres. Creation of permanent posts is a matter for the employer and the same is based on policy decision.
2. While transferring any development project and its manpower to revenue budget the provisions provided in the notifications, government orders and circulars quoted earlier must be followed, However, it is to be remembered that executive power can be exercised only to fill in the gaps and the same cannot and should not supplant the law, but only supplement the law.
3. Before regularization of service of the officers and employees of the development project in the revenue budget the provisions of applicable "Bidhimala" must be complied with. Without exhausting the applicable provisions of the "Bidhimala" as quoted above no one is entitled to be regularised in the service of revenue budget since those are statutory provisions.
4. The appointing authority, while regularising the officers and employees in the posts of revenue budget, must comply with the requirements of statutory rules in order to remove future complication. The officers and employees of the development project shall get age relaxation for participation in selection process in any post of revenue budget as per applicable Rules.
5. A mandamus cannot be issued in favour of the employees directing the government and its instrumentalities to make anyone regularized in the permanent posts as of right. Any appointment in the posts described in the scheduled of Bangladesh Civil Service Recruitment Rules, 1981, Gazetted Officers (Department of Live Stock Service) Recruitment Rules, 1984 and Non-gazetted Employees (Department of Live Stock Service) Recruitment Rules, 1985 by passing Public Service Commission should be treated as back door appointment and such appointment should be stopped.
6. To become a member of the service in a substantive capacity, appointment by the President of the Republic shall be preceded by selection by a direct recruitment by the PSC. The Government has to make appointment according to recruitment Rules by open competitive examination through the PSC.
7. Opportunity shall be given to eligible persons by inviting applications through public notification and appointment should be made by regular recruitment through the prescribed agency following legally approved method consistent with the requirements of law.
8. It is not the role of the Courts to encourage or approve appointments made outside the constitutional scheme and statutory provisions. It is not proper for the Courts to direct absorption in permanent employment of those who have been recruited without following due process of selection as envisaged by the constitutional scheme. In view of the discussion made above and since it is not apparent from the judgment of the High Court Division and other materials available in the record that the procedure provided in the Government notification, circulars
on orders and the process of appointment indicated in the "Bidhimalas" 1995 on 2005 have been followed duly for appointing the, writ petitioners and that they are no longer in service in view of terms of appointment letters and contracts, the direction of the High Court Division to absorb/ regularise their service giving continuity of the same cannot be approved So, the same is set-aside".
9. In the case reported in 72 DLR (AD) 188, it was held,
"When a person enters a temporary employment in the development project or gets engagement as a contractual or casual worker and the engagement is not based on a proper selection as recognised by the relevant rules or procedure, he is aware of the consequences of the appointment being temporary, casual or contractual in nature. Such a person cannot invoke the theory of legitimate expectation for being confirmed in the post when an appointment to the post could be made only by following a proper procedure for selection and in cases concerned, in consultation with the Public Service Commission. Therefore, the theory of legitimate expectation cannot be successfully advanced by temporary, contractual or casual employees. It cannot also be held that the Government has held out any promise while engaging these persons either to continue them where they are or to make them permanent. The Government cannot constitutionally make such a promise. It is also obvious that the theory cannot be invoked to seek a positive relief of being made permanent in the post".
10. It was further held in 72 DLR (AD) 188 that,
"When the employees of the development projects or casual employees appointed as stop-gap arrangement have put in for considerable years of service in the posts and their works have been approved but they could not be regularized, the only provision provides for them is to qualify the requisite examination and in such circumstances, they would get relaxation of upper age limit. If they are not selected, at the end of the day, they would return home from their respective working place with empty hand. It is the duty of the Government/ employers to provide some benefits to them, on the basis of the period of service they rendered, so that they may not fall in extreme hardship otherwise the families of the those employees would face economic ruination.
However, sympathy, empathy or sentiment by itself, cannot be a ground for passing an order where the litigants miserably fail to establish legal right It is true that the respondents had been working for a long time, the same by itself would not be a ground for directing regularization of the service".
11. In Civil Review Petition No. 404 of 2019 which was heard analogously with Civil Review Petition Nos. 7, 30, 42 and 62 of 2020 (judgment on 25-11-2021), the apex Court observed, "In a welfare State a Government by the people and for the people should not return the work-charged employees at the end of the day with empty hand. A political society which has a goal of setting up of a welfare State, should introduce welfare measure wherein benefit is grounded on "considerations of State obligation to its citizens who having rendered service during the useful span of life must not be left to penury in their old age". It is the obligation of the State to take steps so that their lives do not fall in total ruination. For that reason, separate Rules are required to be framed for the persons who have been working as work-charged employees, if necessary, for protecting their future interest so that they do not fall in total disaster at the end of their work."
<u>12. In view of the observations made in 71 DLR (AD) 395 and 72 DLR (AD) 188, it is obvious that the present petitioners cannot claim regularization in the service as a matter of right. Be that as it may, considering the length of service rendered by the petitioners, the concerned authority is at liberty to engage them or continue their engagement in the service as daily basis worker.</u>
With the above observations, the Rule is discharged.
End.

caseno: Civil Appeal No. 316 of 2017 with Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3799 of 2019.
lawyer:
Sk. Md Morshed, Senior Advocate with Sheikh Reajul Hoque, Advocate instructed by Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-record and Madhu Malati Chowdhury Barua, Advocate-on-record—For the Appellants/ petitioners. (In both the cases) 
Md Ruhul Amin Bhuiyan, Advocate instructed by Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-record—For Respondent Nos. 1, 3-4, 6, 8 and 12-15. (In CA No. 316 of 2017)
 Md Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-record—For Respondent Nos. 17-24. (In C.A No. 316 of 2017) 
Md SR Khoshnabish, Advocate-on-record—For Respondent Nos. 2-31. (In C.A No. 316 of 2017) 
Probir Neogi, Senior Advocate instructed by Mohammad Ali Azam, Advocate-on-record—For Respondent No. 36. (In CA No. 316 of 2017) 
None Represented—For Respondent Nos. 2, 5, 7, 9-11, 16, 25-28 and 32-354. (In CA No. 316 of 2017) 
None Represented—For Respondent. (In CP No. 3799 of 2019)
parties:
Razzak Bepari and others……………...Appellants in CA No. 316 of 2017
Md Panchu Dhali and others……………. Petitioners in CP No. 3799 of 2019
VS
Entajuddin and others………………Respondents In both the cases
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 9-7-2015 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 623 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam, J: Delay in filing the Civil Petition for leave to appeal No, 3799 of 2019 is condoned.
2. This civil appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 9-7-2015 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 623 of 1999 making the Rule absolute in part.
3. Short facts are that the predecessors of present respondent Nos.17-34 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.81 of 1994 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Munshigonj for partition of the suit property and declaration that the RS record is wrong in respect of the suit land contending inter-alia that the suit land belonged to ex-landlords Bouddanath Sharma and others, who took khas possession of the suit land from the CS tenant and as they defaulted in paying rent the Zaminder of the suit land by pattan settlement gave to Montazuddin (predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-7), Abdul Hamid (predecessor of plaintiffs) and Mohammad Bepari (predecessor of defendant Nos. 8-10) on 28th Poush of 1362 BS through Amalnama supported by Dakhila. But, in the Amalnama the shares of Montazuddin were wrongly written as 10 annas, 13 gondas, 1 kara, 1 kranti, while that of Abdul Hamid were 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 kranti. The original Amalnama was lost, but photocopy of that was with the plaintiffs. In spite of wrong insertion of shares in the name of Montazuddin, the three settlers possessed the suit land in equal shares and accordingly SA Khatian No.117 was rightly prepared in their names. Abdul Hamid died leaving behind his wife Amina Khatun, who inherited 1/3 share left by Abdul Hamid and she gifted that share equivalent to 0.861/2 acre by two Heba-bil-Ewaz deeds to plaintiff No.1, Md Panchu Dhali and plaintiff No.2 Saifunnessa. Since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by paying rent and mutated their names. The suit land was partitioned by metes and bounds. During RS preparation of record the names of plaintiffs were primarily recorded in the RS khatian Nos.233 and 380, but finally the names of the plaintiffs were omitted. The names of the defendants were recorded in the said RS Khatian omitting the names of the plaintiffs. On the basis of these wrong RS records, the defendants are claiming additional land in which they have no right. So, the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land became clouded. The plaintiffs requested the defendants in the first part of Ashar of 1401 BS for partition, which was denied by the defendants. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the suit.
4. The defendant Nos.1-7 and 8-10 contested the suit by filing separate written statements.
5. Defendant Nos.1-7 contended, inter-alia, that their predecessor Montazuddin took the suit land by pattan/ settlement of 10 annas, 13 gondas, 1 kara, 1 kranti and he also took settlement of remaining 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 karas and 2 krantis in the Benami of Abdul Hamid. Practically Montazuddin was owner of 16 annas, i.e. 2.59 acres of land. Montazuddin paid rent by himself in the Zaminder's Seresta for the entire suit land and had been in possession of the entire suit land by erecting dwelling house and by cultivation. Abdul Hamid never possessed the suit land nor did he pay rent thereof. In the year 1961 Abdul Hamid requested Montazuddin to accord permission for Mohammad Bepari to live in some portion of the suit land and, therefore, Montazuddin permitted Mohammad Bepari to live in a small part of the suit land. In SA khatian, owner Montazuddin, his Benamder Abdul Hamid and licensee Mohammad Bepari's names were recorded. Montazuddin paid rents for the suit land and died leaving defendant Nos.1-7, who had been in possession of the suit land. Before preparation of RS record 10 decimals from plot No.60 and 17 decimals from plot No.63 were occupied by the Government for constructing road and only 1.44 acres of land was recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 1-6 in RS khatian No.223. In order to avoid litigation, the defendants admitted this RS record. The plaintiffs' deeds are forged. Abdul Hamid possessed only 2 annas and he had two wives. So, the plaintiffs cannot claim more than the share inherited by each wife. Defendant Nos.1- 7 possessed 1.44 acres of land. The plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 8-10 have no possession. So, the suit should be dismissed.

6. The defendant Nos. 8-10 contended, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to Zaminder Mohini Kumar Dey and Kangali Dey and they settled the suit land to Mohammad Bepari and put him in possession. At the time of SA record, SA khatian No.117 was correctly made in the name of Montazuddin Morol, Abdul Hamid and Mohammad Bepari. By amicable partition total 2.59 acres of land was possessed by them erecting dwelling houses in equal shares. Mohammad Bepari got 0.86 acre of land in his share. Mohammad Bepari's name was correctly recorded in the RS khatian No.580. Mohammad Bepari died leaving behind 3 sons (defendant Nos.8-10), one daughter Rana Akter and wife Morjina Begum, and the heirs have been possessing 0.82 acre of land by putting pillars and 0.04 acre in ejmali in the pond. The plaintiffs have no title and possession over the suit land. So, the plaintiffs' suit is not maintainable. Defendant Nos. 8-10 prayed for a separate saham of 0.86 acre of land.
7. The trial court decreed the suit for partition on contest in preliminary form against the defendant Nos. 1-7 and 8-10 and ex-parte against the rest. RS khatian No. 223 was also declared wrong and not acted upon. Plaintiffs were given 86.5 decimal of land and defendant Nos. 8-10 were given 86 decimal of land by the preliminary decree.
8. Being aggrieved, defendant Nos.1-7 preferred Title Appeal No.83 of 1996 before the District Judge, Munshigonj challenging that the defendant Nos. 8-10 were not entitled to get any share and RS record No. 223 that was declared wrong is illegal. On transfer the appeal was heard by the Additional District Judge, Munshigonj, who by his judgment and decree dated 8-10-1998 dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Then defendant Nos.1-7 filed Civil Revision No.623 of 1999 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was made absolute in part by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court in Title Appeal No. 83 of 1996 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court. The judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court in Title Suit No. 81 of 1994 so far as it relates to giving 1/3 share of saham to the defendant Nos. 8-10 declaring the RS Khatian No. 223 wrong was also set-aside.
9. Feeling aggrieved the defendant Nos. 8-10 preferred civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division and obtained leave giving rise to this appeal.
10. Mr Sk. Morshed, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court" Division committed error of law in treating the Exhibit 3/Exhibit Ka dated 28 Poush 1362 BS as the Amalnama/Amaldari, that is, the document of title, although on a plain reading of the said exhibit it is apparent that the same is a rent receipt and in any manner it is not a document of title of the predecessors of the plaintiffs or of defendant Nos.1-7, and, as such, the judgment and order passed in Civil Revision No.623 of 1999 is liable to be set-aside.
11. He further submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in mis-appreciating the provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act, in spite of the fact that Exhibit 3/Exhibit ka is not a registered document.
12. He lastly submits that the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute without reversing and discussing the concurrent findings of the courts below regarding possession of the suit land against the respective shares by the parties to the suit, and, as such, the judgment and order dated 7-9-2015 passed in Civil Revision No.623 of 1999 is liable to be struck down.
13. Mr Md Ruhul Amin Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appeared for respondent Nos.1, 3, 4, 6, 8 & 12-15, Mr Md Taufique Hossain, learned Advocate-on-Record appeared for respondent Nos. 17-21, Mr Md SR Khoshnabish, learned Advocate-on-Record appeared for respondent Nos.29-31 and Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Senior Advocate for respondent No. 36 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.
14. We have heard the learned Advocates of both sides at length and perused the impugned decisions together with the papers /documents contained in the paper book.
15. In this case predominant factor is the Amalnama or settlement dated 28 Poush 1362 B.S. which was exhibited by both the plaintiffs and the defendant Nos. 1-7, basing on which the High Court Division held that both the Courts below arrived at a decision on the basis of the Amalnama but failed to consider the names of the parties in the Amalnama which is misreading and non-consideration of the contents of the Amalnama because it clearly shows that the share of Montaz Uddin Morol is 10 annas 13 gonda 1 kara 1 karanti that is 2/3 share and Abdul Hamid Sarder 5 annas 6 gonda 2 kara 2 karanti that is 1/3 share. Furthermore, the Amalnama is an old document produced from proper custody which entitles that the document is genuine. SA and RS records are not document of title and the Amalnama, the document more than 30 years old, shall prevail over the record of rights and would remain in force unless same is cancelled by appropriate civil Court.
16. Believing the said Amalnama the High Court Division finally held that the judgment and decree passed by the court of appeal below affirming the decision of the trial Court giving 1/3 saham to the defendant Nos.8-10 and the declaration that RS Khatian No.223 as wrong are not sustainable in law.
17. Plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 8-10 claimed that actually settlement was taken equally in the name of Montazuddin Morol, Abdul Hamid Sarder and Mohammad Bepari. In spite of wrong insertion of share in the settlement deed Montajuddin Morol, Abdul Hamid Sarder and Mohammad Bepari possessed the suit land in equal shares and during SA operation the SA Khatian No. 117 has rightly been prepared in the names of these three settlers as the owner of the schedule land.
18. The trial court judged that the title and possession of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 8-10 are proved by dint of the oral and documentary evidence adduced therein. It was also proved that the SA khatian No. 117 was correctly recorded in the names of the predecessors of the contesting parties in equal shares. Moreover, possession of defendant Nos. 8-10 and that of the plaintiffs are also admitted by the defendant nos. 1-7. The defendant nos. 1-7 or their predecessor neither protested the separation of jama nor the mutation in the names of the defendant Nos.8-10 regarding the 1/3 portion of the suit land.
19. The High Court Division treating the Exhibit 3 and Exhibit Ka as Amalnama which were exhibited by the plaintiffs and the defendant Nos. 1-7 respectively and held that the Exhibit Ka filed by the defendant Nos. 1-7 is original one and Exhibit 3 filed by the plaintiffs is photo copy of Exhibit Ka which shows that the Amalnama is admitted by the plaintiffs and the defendants. But on plain reading of the said exhibits it is apparent that the same is a rent receipt and in any manner it is not a document of title of the predecessors of the plaintiffs or of defendant Nos.1-7.
20. On the basis of documentary evidences it is proved that the defendant Nos. 1-7 could not establish the settlement to be genuinely a deed of title. And it is evident that the same is a rent receipt having incorporated the essential ingredients of a rent receipt. Moreover, the said rent receipt does not include the name of the predecessor of defendant Nos. 8-10. But, subsequently, during the operation of SA record of rights the defendant Nos. 8-10's predecessor got his name recorded in SA Khatian and strengthen his title in the suit land on par with the predecessors of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-7. The said SA Khatian not being challenged by the predecessors of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-7 had acted upon.
<u>21. Moreso, the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-7 failed to prove that the suit land was recorded during the period of the SA operation on the basis of the alleged settlement/amalnama. Thus, after expiry of nearly about 80 years, we find no reason to believe the so-called settlement as the document of title. However, any amalnama, dakhila and registers of Zamindary period should be believed to be true when SA record would have been published in pursuant to those documents accordingly.</u>
22. So, defendant Nos.8-10 being the successor of the SA recorded tenant Mohammad Bepari, are entitled to get separate saham of 86 decimal in the suit land.
23. In a similar situation in the case of Robert Pinaru vs Moulana Habibur Rahman, 8 MLR (AD) 280 = 8 BLC (AD) 115 it was observed:
"The other contention of the respondent that settlement taken by Taiyab Ali from Charubala as was not established, the plaintiff by purchase from Taiyab Ali in the year 1963 did not acquire any right, title and interest in the land in suit and consequently as the courts below were in error in decreeing the suit the High Court division committed no error in setting aside the said decree is also of no merit as the trial Court as well as the appellate court on consideration of the evidence both oral and documentary, have arrived at the concurrent finding that Taiyab Ali, vendor of the plaintiff took settlement of the land in suit from the admitted owner Charubala it may be mentioned High Court Division while setting aside the decree in the suit failed to advert itself to the materials upon placing reliance whereon the court of first instance and the appellate court arrived at the finding that Taiyab Ali, vendor of the plaintiff took settlement in 1357 BS of the land in suit and in his name SA record was prepared and the plaintiff purchased the land in the year 1963. The High Court division also failed to notice the fact that while settlement to Nurul Islam by charubala in the year 1359 BS was not established as genuine then the claim of the defendant No. 1 in respect of the land in suit by purchase from the person who said to have been taken settlement in 1359 BS did not vest any title in him."
24. In the case of Amanatullah vs Ali Mohammad Bhuiyan, 1997 BLD (AD) 199 = 2 BLC (AD) 134 this Division observed:
"On the second question it is urged by the learned Counsel for the appellants that the High Court Division has acted beyond its jurisdiction in reversing the concurrent findings of fact of the two courts below disregarding the norms of interference. It cannot be gainsaid that a finding of fact, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the lower appellate court is binding on the High Court, as a revisional court except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of material evidence affecting the merit of the case. In this case it does not appear that there is any such error of law in the findings of the trial court and the lower appellate court. It is borne out from the judgment of the lower appellate court in particular that besides the oral evidence the sale deeds and the SA Khatian on the basis of which the rents were alleged to have been paid by the plaintiffs through rent receipts have been duly considered by the said court which is the final court of fact. We are therefore of the opinion that the learned Judges of the High Court Division were not correct in reversing the concurrent decisions of the courts below."
25. In the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Nasia Khatun, 7 BLT (AD) 208 = 5 BLC (AD) 116 it was held that-
"It is long settled that the High Court Division shall not disturb any finding of fact of the appellate court which is based on evidence unless there is any error of law committed by the said court in arriving at a finding and such error has resulted in an error in the decision causing a failure of justice."
26. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute in part without reversing and discussing the concurrent findings of the courts below regarding possession of the suit land against the respective shares by the parties to the suit land.
27. The positive findings of the courts below as mentioned above were wrongly interfered by the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The High Court Division totally misdirected itself in holding that the judgment and decree passed by the learned Judge of the trial Court giving 1/3 saham to the defendant Nos.8-10 and declaration RS Khatian No.223 as wrong are not sustainable in law.
28. In view of the above, we find merit in the appeal.
29. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set-aside. The Judgment of the trial court is restored. The civil petition for leave to appeal No. 3799 of 2019 is disposed of in the light of the judgment delivered in Civil Appeal No. 316 of 2017.
End.
